In the pre-Islamic period, inheritance was based on manhood and strength: they would give inheritance to men to the exclusion of women. Allah, exalted is He, annulled this by His saying: ﴿For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share﴾, as already mentioned. Also in the pre-Islamic period and at the beginning of Islam, inheritance was by *al-muhalafa* (the alliance-pact). Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾, as its explanation will come [[See p. 165 of this part.]]. Then after the alliance, it became by emigration (*hijra*). Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate—you have no guardianship of them until they emigrate﴾ [[See vol. 8, p. 55.]], and it will come. There, if Allah wills, the discussion of the *dhawu al-arham* (blood relatives) and their inheritance will come. In Surat al-Nur [[See vol. 12, p. 195.]] will come the inheritance of the child of the *mula'ana* (the child of the li'an-oath couple) and the child of fornication, and the *mukatab* (slave under a manumission contract), by the power of Allah, exalted is He.

Most scholars hold that the prisoner whose life is known has an inheritance that stands, because he is within the body of Muslims to whom the rules of Islam apply. It has been narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he said regarding a prisoner in the hands of the enemy: he does not inherit. The inheritance of the apostate has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqara [[See vol. 3, p. 49.]]. And praise be to Allah.

**Thirty-first issue:** His saying ﴿without causing harm﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*hal*), and the governing verb is "bequeaths" (*yusa*): he bequeaths it without causing harm, that is, without introducing harm upon the heirs. It is not appropriate for him to bequeath a debt that he does not owe in order to harm the heirs, nor to acknowledge a debt. The harm returns to the bequest and to the debt. As for its return to the bequest: it is by exceeding a third, or by bequeathing to an heir. If he exceeds, it is returned, unless the heirs permit it, because the prohibition is for their rights, not for the right of Allah, exalted is He. If he bequeaths to an heir, it reverts to inheritance. The scholars agreed that a bequest to an heir is not permissible. This was already discussed in Surat al-Baqara [[See vol. 2, p. 257.]]. As for its return to the debt: it is by acknowledgement at a time when it is not permitted to him, as when he acknowledges during his illness a debt to his heir or to an intimate friend; this is not permissible according to us.

It has been narrated from al-Hasan that he recited: ﴿without causing harm, a bequest from Allah﴾ with the genitive construction (*idafa*). Al-Nahhas said: some of the people of language claimed that this is an error, because the active participle is not made to govern a verbal noun in the genitive. The reading is sound with an ellipsis, and the meaning is: "not causing harm to one who has a bequest," that is, not causing harm to his heirs through it in their inheritance. The scholars agreed that his acknowledgement of a debt owed to a non-heir during his illness is permitted, if he did not have a debt in his health.

**Thirty-second issue:** If he had a debt during his health, established by evidence, and he acknowledges a debt to a stranger, then one group said: he begins with the debt of health. This is the view of al-Nakha'i and the Kufans. They said: when the creditor of health has been paid in full, the creditors of the acknowledgement during illness share proportionally. Another group said: they are equal when the creditor is not an heir. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr and Abu 'Ubayd. Abu 'Ubayd mentioned that this is the view of the people of Medina, and it was narrated from al-Hasan.

**Thirty-third issue:** The threat concerning causing harm in a bequest and its aspects has already passed in Surat al-Baqara [[See vol. 2, p. 271.]]. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Shahr ibn Hawshab (and he is criticised) from Abu Hurayra, who related to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a man or a woman may act in obedience to Allah for sixty years, then death comes upon them, and they cause harm in the bequest, so the Fire becomes obligatory for both of them." He said: Abu Hurayra recited to me from here: ﴿after any bequest that is made or a debt, without causing harm﴾, until he reached ﴿That is the great triumph﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: causing harm in a bequest is among the major sins, and he narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ). However, the well-known position of Malik and Ibn al-Qasim is that the testator's act is not considered harm within his third, because that is his right, so he may dispose of it as he wishes. In the school there is another opinion of his: that such an act is harm and is rejected. And with Allah is success.

**Thirty-fourth issue:** His saying ﴿a bequest﴾ (*wasiyya*): it is in the accusative as a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial state (*hal*), and the governing verb is ﴿He enjoins upon you﴾ (*yusikum*). It is also permissible for "without causing harm" to govern it. The meaning is that harm falls upon it or because of it, so the attribution is figurative (*tajawwuz*), as said by Ibn 'Atiyya. It was mentioned that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan recited: ﴿without causing harm a bequest﴾ with the genitive construction, as you say "a brave fighter of war" (*shuja'u harb*). And *bada* (the fair skin) of the bare body is in the words of Tarafa ibn al-'Abd [[*Bada*: fair and soft. "The bare body": her body uncovered from her garments. The verse:
"Wide at the collar of her gown, from her, a companion,
in the restraint of the drinking companions, fair of the bare body."]]. The meaning according to what we have mentioned is figurative speech for the soundness of the meaning. Then He said: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Forbearing﴾, meaning: All-Knowing of the people of inheritance (*ahl al-mirath*) [[In some manuscripts: "All-Knowing regarding the matter of inheritance, All-Forbearing."]], All-Forbearing toward those among you who are ignorant. Some of the earlier readers recited: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [[I have not found this in the non-canonical readings, so it is not to be relied upon.]], meaning: All-Wise in the distribution of inheritance and bequest.

**Thirty-fifth issue:** His saying ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: *tilka* (these) means *hadhihi* (this), that is, these are the rulings of Allah, which He has made clear to you so that you may know them and act by them.

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ in the division of inheritances, acknowledging them and acting by them as Allah, exalted is He, commanded, ﴿He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: this clause is in the accusative position as a qualifier of *jannat* (gardens). His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning in the division of inheritances, so he does not divide them and does not act by them, ﴿and transgresses His limits﴾, that is, opposes His command, ﴿He will admit him into a Fire, to abide therein forever﴾. If by disobedience disbelief is intended, then "abiding forever" is taken in its literal sense; if by it the major sins and the overstepping of Allah's commands are intended, then "abiding" is used figuratively for a certain period, as you say: "May Allah make His dominion eternal (*khallada*)." Zuhayr said:
"Nothing is lasting among the calamities, nor eternal, except the firm mountains."
[[Its first half: "Ala la ara 'ala al-hawadith baqiyan"]]
This meaning has already been discussed in more than one place.

Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿nudkhiluhu﴾ with *nun* in both places, in the sense of attribution to Himself, glorified be He. The rest recited it with *ya'* in both places, because the name of Allah, exalted is He, has already been mentioned.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 15:**

There are eight issues in this verse.

**First:** When God, exalted is He, mentioned in this surah the kindness owed to women and the delivery of their dowries (*sadaqat*) to them, and the matter led on to mentioning their inheritance alongside the inheritance of men, He also mentioned the severity of the penalty for the immorality they might commit, so that a woman would not imagine that it is permissible for her to abandon chastity (*al-ta'affuf*).

**Second:** God's words ﴿wa-llati﴾ (And those who). *Allati* is the plural of *allati* (the feminine relative pronoun), which is an ambiguous noun for the feminine. It is definite, and it is not permissible to remove the *alif* and *lam* from it to make it indefinite. It is not complete without its relative clause (*silah*). It has three dialect forms (*lughat*), as was previously mentioned. It is also pluralized as *al-lat* (by dropping the *ya'* and keeping the *kasrah*), *al-la'i* (with a *hamzah* and retaining the *ya'*), and *al-la'* (with a *kasrah* on the *hamzah* and dropping the *ya'*), and *al-la* (dropping the *hamzah*). If you form the plural of the plural, you say for *allati*: *al-lawati*, and for *al-la'*: *al-lawa'i*. It has also been narrated from them *al-lawat* (dropping the *ya'* and retaining the *kasrah*), as related by Ibn al-Shajari. Al-Jawhari said: Abu Ubayd recited:

*Min al-lawati wa-llati wa-l-lat... za'amna an qad kaburat lidat*
(Of those who are *al-lawati*, *allati*, and *al-lat*, they claim that the age-mates have grown old.)

And *al-lawa* (dropping the *ta'*). The diminutive of *allati* is *al-lutayya* with a *fathah* and a *shaddah*. The rajaz poet said:

*Ba'da al-lutayya wa-l-lutayya wa-l-lati*
(After *al-lutayya*, and *al-lutayya*, and *allati*.)

Some poets added the vocative particle to *allati*, though vocative particles do not enter upon what has the *alif* and *lam*, except in our saying *ya Allah* alone. So it seems that they made it similar to that (*ya Allah*) in that the *alif* and *lam* are inseparable from it. He said:

*Min ajlika ya latti tayyamti qalbi... wa-anti bakhilatun bi-l-wuddi 'anni*
(For your sake, O you who have enslaved my heart, while you are stingy with love toward me.)

It is said: "He fell into *al-latayya* and *allati*," and both are two names among the names of a calamity (*dahiyah*).

**Third:** God's words ﴿ya'tina al-fahisha﴾ (they commit the immorality). *Al-fahisha* in this context means fornication (*zina*). *Al-fahisha* is also any ugly act, and it is a verbal noun (*masdar*), like *al-'aqibah* and *al-'afiyah*. Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿bi-l-fahisha﴾ with the preposition *ba'* of genitive.

**Fourth:** God's words ﴿min nisa'ikum﴾ (from among your women). This is an attribution (*idafah*) that conveys the meaning of Islam and clarifies the condition of believing women, as He said: ﴿wa-stashhidu shahidayni min rijalikum﴾ (and call to witness two witnesses from among your men). This is because a disbelieving woman may be among the women of Muslims by lineage, yet this ruling does not apply to her.

**Fifth:** God's words ﴿fa-stashhidu 'alayhinna arba'atan minkum﴾ (then call four of you as witnesses against them). That is, from among the Muslims. God made the testimony regarding fornication specifically four witnesses, as a severity toward the accuser and a concealment for the servants. The requirement of four witnesses for fornication is a ruling established in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿wa-lladhina yarmuna al-muhsanati thumma lam ya'tu bi-arba'ati shuhada'a fa-jliduhum thamanina jaldatan﴾ (And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes). And here He said: ﴿fa-stashhidu 'alayhinna arba'atan minkum﴾.

Abu Dawud narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Jews brought to the Prophet ﷺ a man and a woman from among them who had committed fornication. He said: "Bring me the two most knowledgeable men among you." So they brought him the two sons of Suriya. He adjured them: "How do you find the matter of these two in the Torah?" They said: "We find in the Torah that if four witnesses testify that they saw his member in her private part like a kohl-stick in a kohl-pot, they are to be stoned." He said: "What prevents you from stoning them?" They said: "Our authority has gone, so we disliked killing." So the Messenger of God ﷺ summoned the witnesses, and they came and testified that they saw his member in her private part like a kohl-stick in a kohl-pot. So the Messenger of God ﷺ ordered that they be stoned.

Some said: The witnesses in fornication were four so that two witnesses would be arranged for each of the two fornicators, as with all other rights, since it is a right that is taken from each of them. This is weak, for the oath enters into property matters and into *lawth* in the *qasamah* (a procedure of oaths in homicide cases), and neither of these has any place here. [[Lawth: it is when one witness testifies to the victim's statement before he died, that so-and-so killed me, or when two witnesses testify to enmity between them or a threat from him toward him, or the like. (Al-Nihayah.)]]

**Sixth:** The witnesses must be males, due to His words ﴿minkum﴾ (from among you), and there is no disagreement among the community (*ummah*) about this. And they must be just (*'udul*), because God, exalted is He, made justice a condition in sales and in revocation of divorce, and this matter is greater, so it is more appropriate for it to be conditioned. This is from applying the unrestricted (*mutlaq*) to the restricted (*muqayyad*) by evidence, as is mentioned in the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*). They must not be *dhimmi* (non-Muslim protected people) [[In Ja: "and not be dhimmiyyah," and in Ta, Ya, and Za: "dhimmah." The intended meaning is the covenanters (mu'ahadun). In al-Bahr: "and not be."]], even if the ruling concerns a *dhimmiyyah* (a female non-Muslim protected person), and this will come in (*Surat al-Ma'idah*). [[See vol. 6, p. 349 onward.]]

Abu Hanifa based his view on God's words ﴿arba'atan minkum﴾ (four of you): that if the husband is one of the witnesses in a charge of slander (*qadhf*), he does not perform *li'an* (mutual oath-cursing). Its explanation will come in (*Surat al-Nur*), God willing, exalted is He. [[See vol. 12, p. 182 onward.]]

**Seventh:** God's words ﴿fa-in shahidu fa-amsikuhunna fi al-buyut﴾ (And if they testify, then confine them to the houses). This was the first of the punishments for fornicators, and it was at the beginning of Islam. This was said by Ubadah ibn al-Samit, al-Hasan, and Mujahid, until it was abrogated (*nusikha*) by the harm (*adha*) that came after it, and then that was abrogated by the verse of *al-Nur* and by stoning for the married (*thayyib*). Another group said: Rather, the harm was the first, and then it was abrogated by confinement, but the recitation was delayed and advanced. This was mentioned by Ibn Furak. This confinement and imprisonment in the houses was at the early period of Islam, before the offenders became numerous. When they increased and their strength was feared, a prison was built for them. This was said by Ibn al-Arabi.

**Eighth:** The scholars differed as to whether this imprisonment was a *hadd* (fixed penalty) or a threat of the *hadd*, on two views. The first: it is a threat of the *hadd*. The second: it is a *hadd*. This was said by Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan. Ibn Zayd added: and they were prevented from marriage until they died, as a punishment for them when they sought marriage in an unlawful manner. This indicates that it was a *hadd*, rather more severe. However, that ruling was limited (*mamdudan*) to an endpoint, which is the harm (*adha*) in the other verse, according to the disagreement among the two interpretations as to which of them came first. Both are extended to an endpoint, which is his peace be upon him saying in the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit: "Take from me, take from me. God has made a way for them. The virgin with the virgin: a hundred lashes and exile for a year. The married with the married: a hundred lashes and stoning." This is like God's words: ﴿thumma atimmu al-siyama ila al-layl﴾ (Then complete the fast until the night). [[See vol. 2, p. 321.]] When the night comes, the ruling of fasting is lifted because its endpoint has ended, not because it was abrogated. This is the view of the verifying later scholars of the principles of jurisprudence, for abrogation (*naskh*) occurs only in two statements that completely contradict each other and cannot be reconciled. Reconciliation is possible between confinement, reproach (*ta'yir*, in another copy: *ta'zir*), flogging, and stoning. Some scholars said: the harm and the reproach (*ta'yir*, in another copy: *ta'zir*) remain alongside the flogging, because they do not contradict each other, but are applied to one person. As for confinement, it is abrogated by consensus (*ijma'*), and the earlier scholars' use of the term "abrogation" for such a case is figurative. And God knows best.

There are seven issues in this (verse).

**First issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the two who commit it among you﴾. (*alladhani*) is the dual of (*alladhi*). The analogical form would have been *al-ladhayani*, like *rahayani* and *mustafayani* and *shajiyyani*. Sibawayh said: the *ya'* was dropped to distinguish between the declinable nouns and the indeclinable nouns (*al-mubhamat*). Abu 'Ali said: the *ya'* was dropped for lightness, since confusion is secure in *alladhani*, because the *nun* is not dropped. The *nun* of the dual in declinable nouns may be dropped with an attached pronoun, as in *rahayaka* and *mustafaya al-qawm*. So if the *ya'* were dropped, the singular would be confused with the dual.

Ibn Kathir recited *alladhani* with a doubled *nun*, which is the dialect of Quraysh. His reasoning is that he made the doubling a substitute for the *alif* of *dha* ("this"), as will be explained in Surah al-Qasas at His saying: ﴿So these two are two proofs﴾ [[See vol. 13, p. 285.]]. There is another dialect, *alladha*, with the *nun* dropped [[In manuscript z: "alladha" with the *nun* dropped; "alladhani" with the *nun* opened. Thus it stands.]]. This is the view of the Kufans. The Basrans said: the *nun* was dropped because the noun is lengthened by the relative clause.

Likewise, he recited *hadhanni* and *fadhanni-ka burhanan* with doubling in both. The rest recited with lightening. Abu 'Amr doubled *fadhanika burhanan* alone.

*Alladhani* is in the nominative as the subject of a sentence. Sibawayh said: the meaning is "and among what is recited to you, those two who come to it," that is, the indecency, "from among you." The *fa'* entered *fa-adhuhuma* because the sentence carries the sense of a command. Since the relative pronoun joined to a verb takes on the sense of a conditional, as no specific thing is determined by it, and since the conditional and the indefiniteness are established in it, it takes the place of the conditional, so the *fa'* enters. The preceding verb does not govern it, just as the preceding word does not govern the conditional. Since it was not good to supply a verb before them in order to put them in the accusative, they were put in the nominative as subjects. This is Sibawayh's preference. The accusative is permissible with a supplied verb, and it is preferred when the sentence carries the sense of command or prohibition, as in your saying: "Those two who are with you, so honour them."

**Second issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so harm them﴾. Qatada and al-Suddi said: its meaning is rebuke and reproach. Another group said: it is abuse and harshness without reproach. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is insulting with the tongue and beating with sandals.

Al-Nahhas said: some people claimed that it was abrogated. I say: Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid that he said: "And those of your women who commit indecency" and "the two who commit it" were at the beginning of the matter, and the verse in al-Nur abrogated both [[See vol. 12, p. 195.]]. This is what al-Nahhas said. It was also said, and it is more preferable, that it is not abrogated, and that it is obligatory that the two be disciplined with rebuke. It is said to them: "You have committed fornication, you have transgressed, and you have opposed the command of Allah, mighty and majestic."

**Third issue:** The scholars differed over the interpretation of His saying: ﴿and those of your women who commit it﴾ and His saying: ﴿and the two who commit it﴾. Mujahid and others said: the first verse concerns women in general, whether married or unmarried, and the second verse concerns men specifically. The dual form distinguishes the two categories of men: the married and the unmarried. So the punishment for women is confinement, and the punishment for men is harm. This view is what the wording requires, and the text covers the categories of fornicators. The wording supports it, as seen in His saying in the first (verse): ﴿of your women﴾, and in the second: ﴿of you﴾. Al-Nahhas chose this view and transmitted it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Qatada, al-Suddi and others said: the first verse concerns married women. This means that married men were included with them by implication. The second verse concerns the virgin man and woman. Ibn 'Atiyya said: the meaning of this view is complete, except that the wording of the verse does not fit it. Al-Tabari preferred it, but al-Nahhas rejected it and said: giving the feminine precedence over the masculine is far-fetched, because a thing is not moved into metaphor when its meaning is valid in its literal sense.

It was also said: confinement was for the adulterous woman and not the man, so the woman was singled out for mention in confinement, then both were combined in harm. Qatada said: the woman was confined and both were harmed, because the man needs to strive and earn a living.

**Fourth issue:** The scholars also differed over acting in accordance with the hadith of 'Ubada, which explains the rulings on fornicators as we have explained. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib acted in accordance with it, and there is no disagreement from him on this. He flogged Shuraha al-Hamdaniyya one hundred lashes and then stoned her. He said: "I flogged her by the Book of Allah and I stoned her by the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy and Ishaq also held this view.

A group of scholars said: rather, the married person is stoned without flogging. This is reported from 'Umar. It is the view of al-Zuhri, al-Nakha'i, Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, the people of opinion, Ahmad and Abu Thawr. They held fast to the fact that the Prophet ﷺ stoned Ma'iz and al-Ghamidiyya [[al-Ghamidiyya with the dotted *ghayn*: a nisba to Ghamid of Juhayna.]] and did not flog them, and to his saying, peace be upon him, to Unays: "Go to this man's wife, and if she confesses, stone her." He did not mention flogging. If it had been prescribed, he would not have remained silent about it.

It was said to them: he remained silent about it because it is established by the Book of Allah, the Exalted. There is nothing preventing him from remaining silent about it because of its fame and because it is explicitly stated in the Qur'an. The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾ covers all fornicators. And Allah knows best.

'Ali's action of taking it from the caliphs, may Allah be pleased with them, confirms this, and no objection was raised against him. It was said to him: "You acted on the abrogated and abandoned the abrogating." This is clear.

**Fifth issue:** They differed over exiling the virgin together with the flogging. The majority hold that the virgin is exiled along with the flogging. This was said by the rightly guided caliphs: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali. It is also the view of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them all. 'Ata', Tawus, Sufyan, Malik, Ibn Abi Layla, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq and Abu Thawr also said so.

Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Abu Hanifa and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan held that it is abandoned. The proof of the majority is the hadith of 'Ubada mentioned above, the hadith of Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid, the hadith of the labourer [[al-'asif (with the unpointed *sin* and *fa'*): the hired labourer.]], in which the Prophet ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will judge between you both by the Book of Allah. As for your sheep and your slave-girl, they are returned to you." He flogged his son one hundred lashes and exiled him for a year. The imams recorded it.

Those who did not hold that exile applies relied on the hadith of Abu Hurayra concerning the female slave, in which only flogging is mentioned and not exile. 'Abd al-Razzaq reported from Ma'mar from al-Zuhri from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: 'Umar exiled Rabi'a ibn Abi Umayya ibn Khalaf for drinking wine to Khaybar. He then joined Heraclius and became a Christian. 'Umar said: "I will not exile a Muslim after this." They said: if exile were a fixed penalty of Allah, the Exalted, 'Umar would not have abandoned it afterwards. Furthermore, the explicit text in the Book prescribes only flogging, and adding to the text is abrogation, so it would follow that a definitive ruling is abrogated by a single report.

The answer: as for the hadith of Abu Hurayra, it concerns slave-women and not free persons. It is authentically reported from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar that he flogged his slave-woman for fornication and exiled her. As for the hadith of 'Umar, his saying "I will not exile a Muslim after this" refers to wine, and Allah knows best. This is because Nafi' reported from Ibn 'Umar that the Prophet ﷺ flogged and exiled, Abu Bakr flogged and exiled, and 'Umar flogged and exiled. It was recorded by al-Tirmidhi in his Jami', and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan, from Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala al-Hamdani, from 'Abd Allah ibn Idris, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from

Nafi'. Al-Daraqutni said: 'Abd Allah ibn Idris alone transmitted it, and no reliable transmitter narrated it from him except Abu Kurayb. Exile is authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ, so no one may argue against it, and whoever opposes the Sunna, I will contend with him. And success is from Allah.

As for their saying that adding to the text is abrogation, this is not conceded. Rather, it is adding another ruling to the original. Furthermore, he [the opponent] added ablution with nabidh [date wine] on the basis of a report that is not authentic over water, and he stipulated poverty for the near kin [[See vol. 8, p. 12.]], and other things not explicitly stated in the Qur'an. This meaning has passed in al-Baqara [[See vol. 2, p. 61.]] and will come again.

**Sixth issue:** Those who hold exile did not differ over exiling a free male. They differed over exiling a male slave and a female slave. Among those who held exile applies to both is Ibn 'Umar, who flogged a female slave of his for fornication and exiled her to Fadak [[Fadak (with a vowel on the *fa'*): a village in the Hijaz between it and Medina, two or three days' journey, according to some. (From Mu'jam al-Buldan.)]]. This is also the view of al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, al-Thawri, al-Tabari and Dawud.

Al-Shafi'i's view on exiling a male slave varied. Once he said: "I seek Allah's guidance regarding exiling a male slave." Another time he said: "He is exiled for half a year." And another time he said: "He is exiled for a year to a place other than his own town." Al-Tabari held this view. His view on exiling a female slave also varied between two opinions.

Malik said: the man is exiled, but the woman and the slave are not exiled. Whoever is exiled is confined in the place to which he is exiled. He is exiled from Egypt to the Hijaz, Shaghb [[As it stands in the originals. Shaghb (with a vowel on the *sh*, then a sukun): a watering place between Egypt and Syria. (From the Qamus.)]], Aswan and similar places, and from Medina to Khaybar and Fadak. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz did likewise. 'Ali exiled from Kufa to Basra. Al-Shafi'i said: the minimum is one day and night.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: the origin of exile is that the people of Isma'il, the best of them, agreed that whoever committed an offence in the sacred precinct would be exiled from it. This became a custom among them which they observed. Because of this, people adopted the practice that whoever committed an offence was exiled from his land. This continued in the Jahiliyya until Islam came and confirmed it for fornication specifically.

Those who did not hold exile applies to male slaves relied on the hadith of Abu Hurayra concerning the slave-woman, and because exiling him is a punishment to his owner, depriving him of his benefits during the period of exile. This does not suit the way the Law operates, since no one other than the offender should be punished. Also, Friday prayer, the pilgrimage and jihad, which are rights of Allah, the Exalted, are waived for the sake of the master, so exile is likewise. And Allah knows best.

When a woman is exiled, it may often be a cause for her to fall into the very thing from which she was removed, namely indecency. Exile also exposes her nakedness and ruins her condition. Furthermore, the basic principle is to prevent her from leaving her house, and her prayer in it is better. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Clothe the women [i.e., strip them of garments fit for going out] so that they stay in the houses" [[*hijal* (sing. *hijla*, with a vowel on the *ha'* and sukun on the *jim*): the plural of *hijla*, meaning the house. That is, strip them of garments for going out so that they remain in their houses.]]. So from this the general wording of the hadith on exile is restricted by a consideration of public interest that has been recognised. This is disputed among the jurists and theorists.

A group deviated and said: flogging and stoning are combined for the married man, and the young man is flogged, relying on the word "old man" in the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The old man and the old woman, if they commit fornication, then stone them outright." Al-Nasa'i recorded it [[As it stands in the originals. This is the narration of al-Bukhari, and in the margin of copy b: a manuscript reads "al-Bukhari". This is the correct version.]]. This is invalid, because in another hadith he called him "the married one" (*al-thayyib*).

The seventh issue: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿If they repent﴾, meaning from the immorality.
(And reform) means doing good deeds afterwards.
(Then leave them alone) meaning: leave off harming them and reproaching them. This was before the revelation of the prescribed punishments (hudud). When the hudud were revealed, this verse was abrogated (nusikhat, naskh). The meaning of "leaving alone" (i'rad) is not boycott (hijra); rather it is abandoning one who turns away, and in it there is a belittling of them because of the earlier sin, and it accords with the ignorance mentioned in the other verse. And Allah is Oft-Returning (tawwab), meaning He turns back toward His servants from their sins.

**Four issues arise from these verses.**

**The first issue: Allah's words, ﴿Repentance is only with Allah﴾.** It has been said that this verse is general, covering everyone who commits a sin. It has also been said that it refers only to one who sins out of ignorance, and that repentance for anyone who commits a sin is mentioned in another place. The community (ummah) agrees that repentance (tawbah) is obligatory for the believers, based on His words: ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers﴾ [24:31]. [See vol. 12, p. 238.]

Repentance from one sin is valid while one persists in another sin of a different kind. This differs from the Mu'tazilah, who say: "One who persists in a sin is not a penitent." They also say there is no difference between one act of disobedience and another. This is the position of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah).

If a servant repents, Allah, glorified is He, has the choice: if He wills, He accepts it, and if He wills, He does not accept it. Accepting repentance is not obligatory upon Allah by reason, as the opponent claims, because a condition of the obligated party is that it must be of higher rank than the one who imposes the obligation upon it. The Truth, glorified is He, is the Creator of creation and its Owner, and the One who imposes duties upon them. Therefore it is not valid to describe Him as being obligated to anything, exalted is He above that. Nevertheless, He, glorified is He, who is truthful in His promise, has informed us that He accepts the repentance of His disobedient servants, by His words: ﴿And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾ [42:25]. [See vol. 16, p. 25 and following.]

His words: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants?﴾ [9:104]. [See vol. 8, p. 250.] And His words: ﴿Indeed, I am Most Forgiving to whoever repents﴾ [20:82]. [See vol. 11, p. 231.] His informing us, glorified and exalted is He, about things that He has made incumbent upon Himself implies the obligation of those things. The creed is that nothing is obligatory upon Him by reason. As for revelation (al-sam'), its apparent meaning is the acceptance of the repentance of the penitent.

Abu al-Ma'ali and others said: "These apparent meanings only convey a strong probability, not certainty regarding Allah's acceptance of repentance." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "Abu al-Ma'ali and others have been opposed in this view." If we suppose a man who has made a sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah) with all its conditions fulfilled, Abu al-Ma'ali said: "It is strongly probable that his repentance is accepted." Others said: "One may be certain that Allah accepts his repentance, just as He has informed us about Himself, Mighty and Majestic is He."

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "My father, may Allah have mercy on him, inclined toward this view and preferred it, and I say the same. Allah, the Exalted, is too merciful to His servants for the meaning of His words ﴿And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ and His words ﴿Indeed, I am Most Forgiving﴾ to be violated concerning this penitent who fulfilled the requirements."

Having established this, know that in His words "with Allah" (ʿalā Allāh) there is an ellipsis, and it is not to be taken literally. The meaning is "by the bounty of Allah and His mercy toward His servants." This is like his (ﷺ) saying to Mu'adh: "Do you know what is the right of the servants upon Allah?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That He should admit them into Paradise." All of this means: "by His bounty and mercy, through His true promise and His truthful word." The evidence is His words: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [6:54], i.e., He promised it. It has also been said that "upon" (ʿalā) here has the meaning of "with" (ʿind), and the meaning is the same: the implied sense is "with Allah," i.e., He has promised, and there is no breaking of His promise, that He accepts repentance when it fulfills the conditions that make it valid. These conditions are four: remorse in the heart, abandoning the sin at once, a firm resolve never to return to its like, and that this be out of shame before Allah, the Exalted, and not before anyone else. If any one of these conditions is lacking, the repentance is not valid. It has also been said that among its conditions is confession of the sin and frequent seeking of forgiveness. Much about the meanings and rulings of repentance has already been mentioned in (Surat) Al 'Imran. [See vol. 4, p. 130.]

As far as I know, there is no disagreement that repentance does not remove a prescribed punishment (hadd). [See vol. 6, p. 174, where the disagreement on this matter is discussed.] For this reason our scholars said: the male thief, the female thief, and the slanderer, when they repent, and when testimony is established against them, the prescribed punishments are carried out upon them.

It has also been said that "upon" (ʿalā) means "from" (min), i.e., "Repentance is only from Allah for those..." This was stated by Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdus. And Allah knows best. The discussion of sincere repentance and the things one repents from will come in (Surat) al-Tahrim. [See vol. 18, p. 197 and following.]

**The second issue: Allah's words, ﴿those who do evil in ignorance﴾.** The word "evil" (al-su') in this verse, and in (Surat) al-An'am where He says: ﴿Whoever among you does evil in ignorance﴾ [6:54], includes disbelief and acts of disobedience. Therefore everyone who disobeys his Lord is ignorant until he desists from his disobedience. Qatadah said: "The companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) agreed that every act of disobedience is done in ignorance, whether it is done deliberately or out of ignorance." Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Mujahid and al-Suddi said the same. It is also narrated from al-Dahhak and Mujahid that they both said: "Ignorance here means deliberate action." Ikrimah said: "All the affairs of this world are ignorance," meaning the particular worldly matters that take one outside obedience to Allah. This statement agrees with His words: ﴿The life of this world is nothing but play and amusement﴾ [47:36]. [See vol. 16, p. 257; vol. 6, p. 414; and vol. 17, p. 254.]

Al-Zajjaj said: "His words ﴿in ignorance﴾ mean their choosing fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure." It has also been said: "in ignorance" means they do not know the reality of the punishment. This was mentioned by Ibn Furak. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: "This view is weak, and it has been refuted."

**The third issue: Allah's words, ﴿Then they repent soon﴾.** Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: "Its meaning is before illness and death." It is narrated from al-Dahhak that he said: "Whatever comes before death is 'soon'." Abu Mijlaz, al-Dahhak also, 'Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd and others said: "Before witnessing the angels and the throes of death (al-sawq) [the throes of death: the extraction, as if the soul is being driven out of the body], and before a person is overpowered by himself."

Mahmud al-Warraq excellently said:

*Send ahead for yourself a hoped-for repentance, before death and before the tongue is bound.*

*Hasten with it, lest the souls be pawned [one says: a pledge is pawned when one cannot redeem it; he means: hasten to repent before the opportunity is lost], for they are a treasure and a gain for the one who turns back and does good.*

Our scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: "Repentance is valid at this time because hope remains, and remorse and a firm resolve to abandon the act are still valid from him." Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn 'Umar that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle (yughargir)." He said: "This is a good, strange hadith." The meaning of "as long as he has not begun the death rattle" is: as long as his soul has not reached his throat, so that it becomes like something gargled. This was stated by al-Harawi. It has also been said: the meaning is that they repent shortly after committing the sin without persisting in it. The one who hastens to repent while healthy is more excellent and closer to what he hopes for than one who does righteous deeds. "Far" (al-bu'd) is completely death, as one says:

*And where is a place of distance except my place?*

This is the second half of a verse by Malik ibn al-Rayb al-Mazini. Its first half is:

*They say: "Do not be far," while they bury me.*

Salih al-Murri narrated from al-Hasan who said: "Whoever reproaches his brother for a sin from which he has repented to Allah, Allah will afflict him with it." Al-Hasan also said: "When Iblis descended he said: 'By Your might, I will not leave the son of Adam as long as the soul is in his body.' Allah, the Exalted, said: 'By My might, I will not withhold repentance from the son of Adam as long as his soul has not begun the death rattle.'"

**The fourth issue: Allah's words, ﴿Nor is repentance﴾.** Allah, glorified is He, has negated that those present at death, at the time of despair, are included in the ruling of penitents, just as Pharaoh, when he was in the surge of water and drowning, was not benefited by what he showed of faith. This is because repentance at that time is of no benefit, since it is a state in which obligation has ceased. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Zayd and the majority of exegetes.

As for disbelievers who die in their disbelief, they have no repentance in the Hereafter, and the reference to them is in His words: ﴿For those We have prepared a painful punishment﴾, which is eternal abiding. If the reference in His words is to all of them, then for the disobedient it is a punishment without eternal abiding, and this is on the basis that the "evil deeds" are what falls short of disbelief. That is, repentance is not for those who did evil deeds short of disbelief and then repented at the time of death, nor for those who died as disbelievers and then repented on the Day of Resurrection. It has also been said: "The evil deeds here are disbelief," so the meaning is: repentance is not for the disbelievers who repent at death, nor for those who die while they are disbelievers.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "The first part of the verse was revealed concerning the believers: ﴿Repentance is only with Allah﴾. The second part concerns the hypocrites."

﴿Nor is repentance for those who do evil deeds﴾: meaning, acceptance of repentance is not for those who persisted in their actions.

﴿Until, when death comes to one of them﴾: meaning, the choking (al-sharaq), the death rattle (al-nazʿ), and witnessing the Angel of Death. [The word translated as choking: in the text, the variant readings differ; some copies read "al-sawq."]

﴿He says: "Indeed I have repented now"﴾: for this there is no repentance.

Then He mentioned the repentance of disbelievers, saying: ﴿Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers, for them We have prepared a painful punishment﴾, meaning, a painful and eternal punishment. This has already been mentioned. [See vol. 1, p. 198.]
