"Men" is the subject and "maintainers" the predicate, meaning that they bear the duty of providing maintenance (nafaqah) for them and defending them. Also, among men are the judges, the rulers, and those who go out to fight, and this is not the case with women. It is said: qiwam and qiyam (both forms of the same root). The verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'[[He is Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' ibn 'Amr ibn Abi Zuhayr ibn Malik ibn Imru' al-Qays al-Khazraji, one who attended the 'Aqabah pledge and Badr, and he was one of the jurists of the Ansar. He had two wives.
(From Usd al-Ghabah.)]]. His wife, Habibah bint Zayd ibn Kharijah ibn Abi Zuhayr, showed defiance towards him, and he slapped her. Her father said: "O Messenger of Allah, I gave him my noble daughter in marriage, and he slapped her!" The Prophet, upon him be peace, said: "Let her take retribution from her husband." So she set out with her father to take retribution from him, but the Prophet, upon him be peace, said: "Return, for this is Jibril who has come to me." Then Allah revealed this verse, and the Prophet, upon him be peace, said: "We intended a matter and Allah intended something else." In another narration: "I intended something, but what Allah intended is better." And he annulled the first ruling. It has been said that in connection with this rejected ruling there was revealed: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾[[See vol. 11, p. 250.]]. Isma'il ibn Ishaq reported, saying: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal and 'Arim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, and the wording is that of Hajjaj, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: A woman came to the Prophet, upon him be peace, and said: "My husband slapped my face." He said: "Between you two is retribution." Then Allah revealed: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾. And the Prophet, upon him be peace, held back until there was revealed: ﴿Men are the maintainers of women﴾.

Abu Rawq said: It was revealed concerning Jamilah bint Ubayy[[In manuscripts b, j, z and t: Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. In Usd al-Ghabah it says: "It is also said she was the daughter of 'Abd Allah, but this is an error."]] and her husband Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning 'Umayrah bint Muhammad ibn Maslamah and her husband Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'. It is also said that its cause was the statement of Umm Salamah mentioned earlier. As for the connection of the verse's composition (nazm) with what precedes: the women spoke about the men being preferred over them in inheritance, so there was revealed: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾, and so on. Then Allah, exalted is He, explained that their preference over them in inheritance is due to what men bear of the dower (mahr) and maintenance, and then the benefit of their preference returns to the women. It is also said that men have a distinction in greater intellect and planning, so the right of maintaining women was given to them on that basis. It has been said that men have a greater strength in soul and disposition than women do, because the nature of men is dominated by heat and dryness, so there is in them strength and vigour, while the nature of women is dominated by moisture and coldness, so there is in them the meaning of softness and weakness. Therefore the right of maintaining them was given to men on that basis, and by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and because they spend from their wealth﴾.

The second: This verse indicates that men discipline their women. When they guard the rights of men, a man should not treat their companionship badly. The word qawwam is an intensive form (fa''al) denoting emphasis, from standing over a thing, exclusively considering it and preserving it with diligence. So men's maintaining of women is on this scale: he takes charge of their affairs, disciplines them, keeps them in their house, and prevents them from going out, and it is incumbent upon her to obey him and accept his command so long as it is not sinful. This ruling is justified by their preference, their maintenance, their intellect, and their strength in the matter of jihad, inheritance, enjoining good, and forbidding evil. Some scholars took beards into account as a basis of preference, but this is nothing, for a beard may exist without any of the things we have mentioned. This refutation has already passed in (al-Baqarah[[See vol. 3, p. 124.]]).

The third: Scholars understood from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and because they spend from their wealth﴾ that whenever a man is unable to maintain his wife, he is not her qawwam, and when he is not her qawwam, she has the right to dissolve the contract, because the purpose for which marriage was legislated has ceased. There is clear evidence in this respect for the validity of annulling a marriage on account of inability to provide maintenance and clothing, and this is the position of Malik and al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifah said: It is not annulled, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if someone is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease﴾[[See vol. 3, p. 371.]]. This matter has already been discussed in this surah.

The fourth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband's absence what Allah has guarded﴾. All of this is a statement of fact, but its intended meaning is a command to obey the husband and to uphold his rights concerning his property and concerning herself in his absence. In the Musnad of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, upon him be peace, said: "The best of women is she who, when you look at her, pleases you, when you command her she obeys you, and when you are absent from her she guards you in herself and your property." He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿Men are the maintainers of women﴾ to the end of the verse. The Prophet, upon him be peace, also said to 'Umar: "Shall I not inform you of the best thing a man can treasure? A righteous wife: when he looks at her, she pleases him; when he commands her, she obeys him; and when he is absent from her, she guards him." Abu Dawud related it.

In the codex (mushaf) of Ibn Mas'ud it reads: ﴿So the righteous women are qawanit, hawafiz﴾[[In the Shawadh of Ibn Khalawayh it is the recitation of Talhah ibn Musarrif.]]. This is a pattern specific to the feminine. Ibn Jinni said: The broken plural (taksir) is more fitting in wording to the meaning, since it conveys plurality, and plurality is what is intended here. In His saying: ﴿bima hafiza Allah﴾ the "ma" is verbal-masdariyyah, meaning "by Allah's guarding of them." It may also be taken to mean "that which," and the returning pronoun in "hafiza" would then be an object pronoun. In the recitation of Abu Ja'far, it is read ﴿bima hafiza Allah﴾ with a fatha (naṣb). Al-Nahhas said: The nominative reading is clearer, meaning: guarding, by Allah's guarding and His aid and His support, the absence of their husbands[[Ta-sdidahu in manuscripts j, b, z and d, from al-sadad (rectitude).]]. It is also said: "by what Allah has entrusted them with concerning their dowries" and their marital life. It is also said: "by what Allah has made them guardians of, namely the discharge of trusts to their husbands." The meaning of the accusative reading is: "by their guarding Allah," that is, by their guarding His command or His religion. It is also said in the interpretation: "by what they guarded of Allah," and then the verb is made singular, as it has been said:

"Indeed, the calamities have harmed them"[[He means: harmed by them. (From al-Bahr.)]]

It is said: the meaning is "by the protection of Allah," like "I sought Allah's protection" (ḥafiztu Allāh).

Fifth: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz (rebellion)﴾. Allati is the plural of allati, which has already been discussed. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "takhafun" here means "you know and are certain." It is also said that it retains its original meaning. Nushuz is disobedience, derived from al-nashz, which is what rises above the ground. One says: nashaza al-rajul yanshuzu and yanshizu, when he was sitting and then stood up. From this is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: (And when it is said, "Rise up, so rise up")[[See vol. 17, p. 299]], meaning: rise and stand up for war or for a matter of the affairs of Allah, exalted is He. So the meaning is: you fear their disobedience and their haughtiness against what Allah has made obligatory upon them of obedience to their husbands. The lexicographer Abu Mansur said: nushuz is the mutual aversion of each of the spouses to the other. One says: nashazat tanshuzu, so she is nashiz without a taʾ (hā'). And nashasat tanshusu, and she is the one who is bad for companionship. Ibn Faris said: "nashazat al-mar'ah" means the woman became difficult for her husband to manage, and "nashaza baʿluha ʿalayha" means when he struck her and treated her harshly. Ibn Durayd said: nashazat al-mar'ah, nashasat, and nashasat have one meaning.

Sixth: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Then admonish them﴾, meaning with the Book of Allah; that is, remind them of what Allah has made obligatory upon them of good companionship and fine conduct toward the husband, and of acknowledging the degree that he has over them. And he says: The Prophet ﷺ said: "If I were to order anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would order the woman to prostrate to her husband." And he said: "She should not refuse him herself even if she is on the back of a saddle [[al-qatab (with vowel) is a saddle for a camel, like the kaf (pack-saddle) and the barda'a (saddle-cloth) for other animals. Its meaning is an exhortation to them to obey their husbands, and that it is not permissible for them to refuse in the present situation, let alone in others.]]." And he said: "Any woman who spends the night refusing her husband's bed, the angels curse her until morning," and in another narration, "until she returns and places her hand in his hand." And what is similar to this.

Seventh: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And forsake them in the beds﴾. Ibn Masʿud, al-Nakhaʿi and others read (fī al-maḍjaʿ) in the singular, as if it were a collective noun that serves for the plural. Hajr in the beds is that he lies with her and turns his back to her and does not have intercourse with her, according to Ibn ʿAbbas and others. Mujahid said: "avoid their beds." In this view, there is an ellipsis in the sentence, and it is supported by (uhjurūhunna), from al-hijran, which is distance. One says: hajarahu, meaning he kept away from him and stayed far from him. Her distance cannot be achieved except by abandoning lying with her. Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, al-Shaʿbi, Qatadah and al-Hasan al-Basri said the same meaning, and Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Qasim related it from Malik, and Ibn al-ʿArabi chose it and said: "They applied the command to the most common and complete sense." This view is like your saying: "forsake him for the sake of Allah." This is the principle of Malik. I say: this is a good view, for when the husband turns away from her bed, if she loves the husband, that is hard for her, so she returns to goodness; and if she hates him, then the nushuz manifests from her, and it becomes clear that the nushuz is from her side. It is also said: (uhjurūhunna) is from hajr, which is ugly speech; that is, be harsh with them in speech, and lie with them for intercourse and other purposes. Sufyan said this meaning, and it was related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It is also said: that is, tie them with a rope in their houses, from the saying "hajara al-baʿir," meaning he tied the camel with a hijar, which is a rope with which a camel is tied. This is the choice of al-Tabari, and he disparaged all the other views. There is scrutiny in his words on this point. Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-ʿArabi refuted him in his Aḥkām, saying: "What a blunder from a scholar of the Qur'an and the Sunnah!" What led him to this interpretation is a rare ḥadīth related by Ibn Wahb from Malik, that Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, the wife of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam, used to go out until she was reproached for that. He said: He was angry with her and with her co-wife, so he tied the hair of one to the other, then struck them both severely. The co-wife was better at protecting herself, while Asma' did not protect herself, so the striking fell more on her. She complained to her father Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said to her: "O my daughter, be patient, for al-Zubayr is a righteous man, and perhaps he will be your husband in Paradise. It has reached me that when a man takes a woman as a first wife, he marries her in Paradise." So he saw the tying and the knotting, with the possibility of the wording, together with al-Zubayr's action, and so he adopted this interpretation. This hajr, according to the scholars, reaches at most a month, as the Prophet ﷺ did when he confided to Hafsah and she disclosed it to ʿAʾishah, and both of them backed each other against him. It does not extend to four months, which Allah set as the term that is an excuse for the one who swears off (ilaʾ).

Eighth: His saying, ﴿and strike them﴾. Allah commanded that women should first be started with admonition, then with forsaking, and if these do not work, then striking, for it is what sets her right and moves her to fulfill his right. The striking in this verse is the striking of discipline that is not severe, which does not break a bone nor disfigure a limb, such as a light push and the like, for its purpose is only correction. Therefore, if it leads to death, compensation is required. The same applies to a teacher's striking his student for teaching the Qur'an and good conduct. In Sahih Muslim: "Fear Allah concerning women, for you have taken them under the trust of Allah and made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah. You have the right over them that they do not let anyone you dislike tread on your bedding. If they do that, then strike them with a striking that is not severe..." the ḥadīth. He related it from the long ḥadīth of Jabir in the chapter on Hajj. That is, they should not let into your homes anyone you dislike, from relatives and foreign women[[In ʿ, w, z: "wa-al-ajanib."]]. On this is understood what al-Tirmidhi related and authenticated from ʿAmr ibn al-Aḥwas, that he witnessed the Farewell Pilgrimage with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he praised Allah, extolled Him, reminded and admonished, and said: "Beware! Treat women well, for they are like captives with you; you own nothing from them except that, unless they commit a clear immorality. If they do, then forsake them in the beds and strike them with a striking that is not severe. If they obey you, then do not seek a way against them. Beware! You have a right over your women, and your women have a right over you. As for your right over your women, they should not let anyone you dislike tread on your bedding, nor allow anyone you dislike into your houses. Beware! Their right over you is that you treat them well in their clothing and food." He said: this is a good, sound ḥadīth. So his saying, "with a clear immorality," means they should not let in anyone their husbands dislike, nor anger them. The intended meaning is not adultery, for that is forbidden and would require the hadd punishment. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Strike women if they disobey you in what is good, with a striking that is not severe." ʿAtaʾ said: I said to Ibn ʿAbbas, "What is striking that is not severe?" He said: "With a miswak or the like." It is related that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, struck his wife and was blamed for that, and he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'A man is not asked why he struck his family.'"

Ninth: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿If they obey you﴾, meaning they abandon nushuz.
(then seek not a way against them), meaning do not wrong them by word or deed. This is a prohibition against oppressing them after establishing your superiority over them and granting you the means of disciplining them. It is also said: the meaning is, do not burden them with loving you, for that is not in their power.

Tenth: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand﴾. This is an indication to the husbands to lower the wing and be gentle. That is, if you are inclined to overpower them, then remember Allah's power, for His hand is over every hand with power. So no one should exalt himself over his wife, for Allah is ever watchful. Therefore, the attributes of highness and greatness are fittingly mentioned here.

Eleventh: When this is established, know that Allah, mighty and majestic, did not command striking explicitly anywhere in His Book except here and in the grave hudud. He equated their disobedience toward their husbands with the disobedience of major sins, and entrusted this matter to the husbands rather than the rulers, and made it theirs rather than the judges, without witnesses or proofs, as a trust from Allah, exalted is He, given to husbands over wives. Al-Muhallab said: striking women was only permitted because of their refusing their husbands in intercourse. There is a difference of opinion on whether striking them for service is obligatory, and analogy requires that if striking her for intercourse is permitted, then striking her for the service that is owed to the husband by her in accordance with what is customary is also permitted. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: nushuz cancels maintenance and all marital rights, and with it the husband may discipline her with a discipline that is not severe, and admonish and forsake her until she returns from her nushuz; when she returns, her rights return. Likewise, whatever calls for discipline is permitted for the husband to discipline her with. The situation differs regarding the discipline of a noble woman and a lowly one: the discipline of a noble woman is reproach, and the discipline of a lowly one is the whip. The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who hangs up his whip and disciplines his family." He also said: "Abu Jahm does not lay down his staff from his shoulder." Bashshar said:

The free man is reproached, and the staff is for the slave.

"Yulha" means "is blamed." Ibn Durayd said:

Blame remains a deterrent for the free man... and only the staff deters the slave.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: the scholars agreed that the maintenance of wives is obligatory upon their husbands when they are all adults, except a wife who is nashiz and refusing. Abu ʿUmar said: whoever's wife becomes nashiz toward him after consummation, her maintenance falls from him, unless she is pregnant. Ibn al-Qasim differed from the majority of jurists regarding the maintenance of a nashiz and made it obligatory. When the nashiz returns to her husband, her maintenance becomes obligatory for the future. A woman's maintenance does not fall from her husband for any reason other than nushuz: not because of illness, menstruation, postpartum bleeding, fasting, pilgrimage, the husband's absence, or his being detained away from her for a right or an injustice, beyond what we have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

There are five issues in this.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾. The meaning of shiqaq (breach, discord) has already been explained in al-Baqarah (see vol. 1, p. 464, and vol. 2, p. 341). It is as if each of the spouses takes a side (shiqq) other than the side of his companion, that is, a direction other than that of his companion.

The intended meaning is: if you fear a breach between them. The verbal noun is then idafa (annexed) to the adverb of place, as when you say: "The journey of the moonlit night pleases me," and "the fasting of the day of 'Arafah." And in the revelation: ﴿Nay, but the scheming of the night and the day﴾ (vol. 14, p. 301). It has also been said that bayn (between) is treated as a noun, its adverbial sense removed from it, since it means their state and their companionship, that is: "And if you fear the estrangement of their companionship and their association." (So send). The word "you fear" is subject to the difference of opinion mentioned earlier (see p. 11 of this part).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The ruling is that he should first admonish her; if she accepts, well and good, otherwise he should forsake her (in bed); if she accepts, well and good, otherwise he should strike her. If she accepts, well and good, otherwise the judge shall send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family, and they shall examine who is the source of the harm. At that point, khul' (divorce by wife's request) takes place. It has also been said that he may strike her before admonishing her, but the first view is more correct because of the order in which this is arranged in the verse.

The second: The majority of scholars hold that the addressees of His saying "And if you fear" are the judges and rulers, and that His saying "If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring them together" refers to the two arbiters, according to the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others; that is, if the two arbiters desire reconciliation, Allah will bring the spouses together. It has also been said that the intended meaning is the spouses themselves: if the spouses desire reconciliation and sincerity regarding what they reported to the two arbiters, "Allah will bring them together." It has also been said that the address is to the guardians (awliya'); he says: "If you fear" meaning if you know of a dispute between the spouses, "then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family." The two arbiters must be from the family of the husband and the wife, since they are most knowledgeable about the circumstances of the spouses, and they should be from among those who are upright, of good judgment, and skilled in jurisprudence. If none of their families is found suitable for this, then two just and learned persons are sent from outside them. This applies when their situation is unclear and it is not known which of them is at fault. As for when the wrongdoer is known, his right is taken from his companion and he is compelled to remove the harm. It is said that the arbiter from the husband's family is alone with him and says: "Tell me what is in your heart: do you desire her or not, so that I may know your intention?" If he says: "I have no need of her; take from her what you can and separate me from her," then it is known that the nushuz (disobedience) is from his side. If he says: "I desire her, so satisfy her from my wealth as you wish, and do not separate me from her," then it is known that he is not a nashiz. The arbiter from her side is alone with the woman and says: "Do you desire your husband or not?" If she says: "Separate me from him and give him from my wealth what he wants," then it is known that the nushuz is from her side. If she says: "Do not separate us, but urge him to increase my maintenance and to treat me well," then it is known that the nushuz is not from her side. When it becomes clear to both of them which of them was the source of the nushuz, they address that one with admonition, rebuke and prohibition. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾.

The third: The scholars said: this verse divides women by rational division, for they are either obedient or nashiz, and nushuz either returns to obedience or it does not. If it is the first, they are left alone, based on what al-Nasa'i narrated: that 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib married Fatimah bint 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, and whenever he entered upon her she would say: "O sons of Hashim, by Allah my heart will never love you! Where are those whose necks are like silver ewers! Their noses are turned back before their lips! Where is 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, where is Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah?" He would remain silent about her, until one day he entered upon her while he was angry, and she said to him: "Where is 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah?" He said: "On your left in the Fire when you enter it." So she gathered her garments around her and went to 'Uthman and told him of that. He sent Ibn 'Abbas and Mu'awiyah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I will surely separate them." Mu'awiyah said: "I would not separate two elders of the sons of 'Abd Manaf." They came to them and found that they had shut their doors upon them and had reconciled their affair. If they found them still in disagreement, not reconciled, and their affair had grown worse, they would strive for harmony with all their effort, and remind them of Allah and of companionship. If they repented and returned, they would leave them alone; but if they were otherwise and saw that separation was best, they would separate them. Their separation is permissible for the spouses, whether it agrees with the ruling of the city's judge or opposes it, whether the spouses appointed them for this or did not appoint them. Such separation is an irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in). Some people said: they have no authority to divorce unless the husband has delegated them in this matter, and they should inform the imam. This is based on the view that they are two witnesses or messengers. Then the imam separates them if he wishes, and orders the arbiter to separate them. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, and the Kufans held it, and it is the view of 'Ata', Ibn Zayd and al-Hasan, and Abu Thawr also held it. The sound view is the first: that the two arbiters have the authority to divorce without delegation. This is the view of Malik, al-Awza'i and Ishaq, and it is related from 'Uthman, 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas, and from al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾, and this is an explicit statement from Allah, glorified is He, that they are judges, neither agents nor witnesses. The agent (wakil) has a name and meaning in the sharia, and the arbiter (hakam) has a name and meaning in the sharia; when Allah has clarified each of them, it is not fitting for an anomalous view, let alone a scholar, to superimpose the meaning of one upon the other! Al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Sirin from 'Ubaydah concerning this verse ("And if you fear a breach between the two, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family"), he said: A man and a woman came to 'Ali, each with a large group (fi'am) of people. He ordered them, and they sent an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. He said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what is upon you? Upon you, if you see that you should separate them, you shall separate them." The woman said: "I am content with the Book of Allah, with what is upon me and what is mine in it." The husband said: "As for separation, no." 'Ali said: "You lie, by Allah you shall not leave until you acknowledge the like of what she acknowledged." This is a sound, established chain, related from 'Ali through established channels from Ibn Sirin from 'Ubaydah. Abu 'Umar said: If they were agents or witnesses, he would not have said to them: "Do you know what is upon you?" He would only have said: "Do you know with what you have been appointed?" And this is clear. Abu Hanifa argued with 'Ali's saying, may Allah be pleased with him, to the husband: "You shall not leave until you are content with what she was content with." This shows that his view is that they do not separate except with the husband's consent, and because the established principle is that divorce is in the hand of the husband or in the hand of whomever he has delegated it to. Malik and those who followed him placed it under the category of the ruler's divorce on the walī (guardian) and the impotent man.

The fourth: If the two arbiters disagree, their word does not take effect, and nothing is binding except what they both agree upon. Likewise, any two arbiters who give a ruling on a matter: if one of them rules for divorce and the other does not rule for it, or if one rules for property and the other refuses, then they are nothing until they agree. Malik said concerning the two arbiters who pronounce three divorces: one is binding (tulzamu, "it shall be binding"); and they have no authority to separate beyond one irrevocable divorce. This is the view of Ibn al-Qasim. Ibn al-Qasim also said: the three are binding on him if they both agree upon them. Al-Mughirah, Ashhab, Ibn al-Majishun and Asbagh held this. Ibn al-Mawwaz said: if one of them rules for one and the other for three, it is one. Ibn Habib related from Asbagh that this is nothing.

The fifth: It is permissible to send a single person, because Allah, glorified is He, ruled concerning adultery by four witnesses; yet the Prophet ﷺ sent Unays alone to the adulterous woman and said to him: "If she confesses, then stone her." Likewise 'Abd al-Malik said in the Mudawwana.

I say: if it is permissible to send one person, then if the spouses appoint a single arbiter (ḥakam), it suffices, and it is even more permissible when they both consent to that. God addressed the sending of arbiters to the rulers (al-ḥukkām), not to the spouses. If the spouses send two arbiters and they issue a ruling, their ruling is enforced, because arbitration (taḥkīm) is valid in our school, and the act of the arbiter is enforced in every matter. This applies when each of them is just (ʿadl). If one of them is not just, ʿAbd al-Malik said: his ruling is annulled, because they have gambled (takhāṭarā) on something improper, which is uncertain risk (gharar).

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: The correct view is that it is enforced, because if it is an appointment of an agent (tawkīl), then the act of the agent is binding; and if it is arbitration, then they have referred the matter to themselves, and the uncertainty does not affect it, just as it does not affect the chapter on agency. The chapter on judgeship is built entirely on uncertainty, and it is not required that the person against whom the ruling is issued know what the ruling will lead to.

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: The matter of the two arbiters is one that God explicitly stated and ruled upon when discord (shiqāq) appeared between the spouses and their differences grew. It is a great matter on whose basic principle the community (umma) agrees regarding sending (al-baʿth), although they differ over the details of what follows from it. How strange are the people of our land, who neglected what the Book and the Sunna require in this and said: "They shall be placed in the hands of a trustworthy person." In this there is an opposition to the explicit text that is not hidden from you. They did not follow the Book of God, nor did they content themselves with analogies (aqyisa). I urged them to this, but no one responded to me in sending the two arbiters at the time of discord except one judge, nor in judging by the oath together with a witness except another. When God gave me authority over the matter, I implemented the Sunna as it should be. Do not be surprised at the people of our land because ignorance has overwhelmed them [[كذا في ابن العربي. وفى الأصول: لما عندهم.]], but be surprised at Abu Hanifa, who has no report (khabar) concerning the two arbiters, and be surprised twice at al-Shafiʿi, for he said: "What resembles the apparent meaning of the verse is that it concerns matters that involve both spouses together, to the point that their two conditions become unclear." He said: "That is because I found that God, mighty and majestic, permitted reconciliation (iṣlāḥ) when the husband is disobedient (nushūz), and permitted, when they fear that they will not keep the limits of God, khul‘ (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), and that resembles being with the wife's consent. He prohibited the husband from taking anything of what he gave when he wishes to replace one spouse with another. So when He commanded the sending of two arbiters for those between whom we fear discord, this indicates that their ruling is other than the ruling of the spouses. If that is so, he sends an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers, and they send the two arbiters only as trustworthy persons, with the consent of the spouses and their delegation to them, that they may unite or separate when they see fit. This indicates that the two arbiters are agents (wakīlān) of the spouses."

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: This is the end of al-Shafiʿi's statement. His followers rejoice in it, yet there is nothing in it worth attention, and it does not match his standing in knowledge. al-Qadi Abu Ishaq undertook the refutation of it, but he was not fair to it in most of its points. As for his statement, "What resembles the apparent meaning of the verse is that it concerns matters that involve both spouses," it is not correct; rather, it is an explicit text, and it is among the clearest and most evident verses of the Qur'an, for God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾. Whoever fears disobedience (nushūz) from his wife should admonish her; if she repents, well and good, otherwise he should abandon her in the bed; if she mends her ways, well and good, otherwise he may strike her; if she persists in her defiance, the two arbiters go to them both. If this is not an explicit text, then there is no clarity in the Qur'an. Leave aside that it is not explicit, let it be apparent. But as for al-Shafiʿi saying "it resembles the apparent meaning," we do not know what it resembles of the apparent meaning. Then he said: "He permitted, when they fear that they will not keep the limits of God, khul‘, and that resembles being with the wife's consent," rather, it must be so, and this is his explicit text. Then he said: [[?]] "When He commanded the arbiters, we knew that their ruling is other than the ruling of the spouses, and it must be other than that, by its being enforced upon them without their choice, so that otherness is realized. As for when they enforce upon them what the spouses delegated to them, and they do not rule contrary to their command, then otherness is not realized." As for his statement "with the consent of the spouses and their delegation," it is a clear error, for God, glory be to Him, addressed other than the spouses when He feared discord between the spouses, by sending the two arbiters. When the one addressed is other than them, how can it be by their delegation? Nor is any ruling valid for them except what they both agree upon. This is the approach of fairness and precision in refuting him. In this verse there is evidence for establishing arbitration (taḥkīm), and it is not as the Khawārij say, that arbitration belongs to no one except God, the Exalted. This is a word of truth [but [[من ج وط، ز، د. يريدون ما حكم الا فيه لأغير.]]] by which they intend falsehood.

There are eighteen issues in it.

**The first issue:** The scholars agreed unanimously that this verse is among the *muhkam* (decisive, clear verses) on which there is consensus, and that none of it has been abrogated (*mansukh*). It is likewise in all the (earlier) Books. Even if this were not so, it would be known by reason, even if the Book had not revealed it. The meaning of *ʿubudiyyah* (worship/servitude) has already passed: it is humbling oneself and being in need, before the One to whom belongs judgment and choice. So Allah the Exalted commanded His servants to humble themselves before Him and to be sincere in it. The verse is therefore a foundation for the sincerity of deeds for Allah the Exalted and for purifying them from the taints of *riyaʾ* (showing off) and other things. Allah the Exalted said: (So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.) [See vol. 11, p. 64.] To the point that some of our scholars said: whoever performs ablution to cool himself down, or fasts to relieve his stomach's heat, and at the same time intends drawing near (to Allah), it will not suffice him, because he has mixed a worldly intention into the intention of drawing near, and for Allah there is only pure deed. As Allah the Exalted said: (Is it not for Allah that the pure religion belongs?) [See vol. 15, p. 232.] And He said: (And they were commanded only to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion) [See vol. 20, p. 144]. Likewise, if a man perceives someone entering into bowing (*rukuʿ*) while he is leading the prayer, he should not wait for him, because by waiting he takes his bowing out of being purely for Allah the Exalted.

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'I am the most independent of partners from association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his partner.'" Al-Daraqutni also narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, sealed scrolls will be brought and placed before Allah the Exalted. Allah the Exalted will say to the angels: 'Throw this away and accept this.' The angels will say: 'By Your might, we have seen nothing but good.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say—and He knows best—'This was for other than Me, and I do not accept today any deed except what was sought by it My Face.'" It is also narrated from al-Dahhak ibn Qays al-Fihri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'I am the best partner. Whoever associates a partner with Me, it belongs to My partner. O people, make your deeds sincere for Allah the Exalted, for Allah accepts only what is sincere to Him. Do not say "This is for Allah and for the relatives," for it is for the relatives and nothing of it is for Allah. Do not say "This is for Allah and for your faces," for it is for your faces and nothing of it is for Allah the Exalted.'"

**Issue:** Having established this, know that our scholars, may Allah be pleased with them, said: *Shirk* (associating partners with Allah) has three levels, and all of it is forbidden. Its root is believing in a partner with Allah in His divinity (*ulūhiyyah*), and this is the greatest *shirk*, the *shirk* of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period), and it is what is meant by His saying: (Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills). Next in rank is believing in a partner with Allah in action, which is the saying of one who says that some existent other than Allah can independently bring about an act and originate it, even if he does not believe it to be a god, like the Qadariyyah, the Magians of this nation. Ibn Umar disassociated himself from them, as in the Hadith of Jibril, peace be upon him. Following this rank is associating others in worship, which is *riyaʾ*: doing some of the acts of worship that Allah commanded to be done for Him, but doing them for someone else. This is what the verses and Hadiths were brought to explain the prohibition of, and it nullifies deeds. It is hidden, and no foolish ignoramus recognizes it. May Allah be pleased with al-Muhasibi, for he clarified it in his book *al-Riʿayah* and explained how it corrupts deeds.

In Sunan Ibn Majah, from Abu Saʿid ibn Abi Fadalah al-Ansari, who was among the Companions, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last for the Day of Resurrection, the Day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: whoever associated anyone else in a deed he did for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, let him seek its reward from other than Allah, for Allah is the most independent of partners from association."

Also in it, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us while we were discussing the Dajjal (the Antichrist), and he said: "Shall I not inform you of what I fear for you more than the Dajjal?" He said: We said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Hidden *shirk*: that a man stands to pray and beautifies his prayer because he sees a man looking at him."

Also in it, from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, what I fear most for my Ummah is *shirk* with Allah. Behold, I am not saying they will worship a sun or a moon or an idol, but (they will do) deeds for other than Allah, and hidden desire." Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated it. It will come in the end of *al-Kahf* [see vol. 11, p. 69], and in it is an explanation of hidden desire. Ibn Lahiʿah narrated from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about hidden desire, and he said: "It is a man who learns knowledge and loves that people sit with him."

Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Tustari, may Allah be pleased with him, said: *Riyaʾ* has three aspects. The first: he establishes in the origin of his act something for other than Allah, and he wants by it to be known as doing it for Allah. This is a type of hypocrisy (*nifaq*) and doubt in faith. The second: he enters into the act for Allah, but when someone other than Allah observes him, he becomes energetic. This one, if he repents, should repeat everything he did. The third: he enters into the act with sincerity and leaves it for Allah, so he is recognized by it and praised for it, and he is calmed by their praise. This is the *riyaʾ* that Allah forbade.

Sahl said: Luqman said to his son: "*Riyaʾ* is that you seek the reward of your deed in the worldly life, whereas the deeds of the people are for the Hereafter." He was asked: "What is the cure for *riyaʾ*?" He said: "Concealing the deed." He was asked: "How is the deed concealed?" He said: "What you are not obligated to display of deeds, do not enter into except with sincerity; and what you are not obligated to display, prefer that no one observe it except Allah." He said: "And every deed that people have observed, do not count it as a deed."

Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani said: "He is not intelligent who loves that others know his standing in his deed."

I say: Sahl's saying "And the third entered into the deed with sincerity..." to its end: if his calm and joy in them is so that his status will be attained in their hearts, that they will praise him, honour him, and clear him, and he obtains from them what he wants of wealth or other things, then this is blameworthy, because his heart is overwhelmed with joy at their observing it, even if they observed it only after he finished. As for the one whom Allah has made his creatures observe while he does not love their observing it, and he is glad at Allah's doing and His favour upon him, then his joy at Allah's favour is obedience, as Allah the Exalted said: (Say: "By the bounty of Allah and His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate.") [See vol. 8, p. 353.] The elaboration and completion of this is in al-Muhasibi's *al-Riʿayah*, so whoever wants it should consult it there.

Sahl was asked about the Hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I conceal the deed, then it is observed, and it pleases me." He said: "It pleases him from the aspect of thanks to Allah, who made it manifest to him," or something like this.

This is a sufficient summary on *riyaʾ* and the sincerity of deeds. It has passed in (*al-Baqarah*) [see vol. 2, p. 146] the reality of sincerity (*ikhlas*). And praise be to Allah.

**The second issue:** His saying: ﴿And to parents, good treatment﴾. It has already been mentioned at the beginning of this surah that among kindness to them is freeing them (from slavery). The rule of their righteousness will come fully in (*Subhan*) [see vol. 10, p. 236]. Ibn Abi ʿAblah read *iḥsānun* with *raf*ʿ (nominative), meaning kindness to them is obligatory. The rest read it with *nasb* (accusative), meaning: "Be kind to them, a kindness." The scholars said: The most deserving of people, after the Creator, the Bestower, of thanks, kindness, adherence to righteousness and obedience, and submission, are those whom Allah linked kindness to them with His worship, obedience to Him, and thanking Him with thanking them, and they are the two parents. He said: (Give thanks to Me and to your parents) [see vol. 14, p. 63].

Shuʿbah and Hushaym al-Wasitiyyan narrated from Yaʿla ibn ʿAta, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Lord's pleasure is in the parents' pleasure, and His wrath is in the parents' wrath."

**The third issue:** His saying: ﴿And to the near relative, the orphans, and the needy﴾. The discussion of it has passed in (*al-Baqarah*) [see vol. 2, p. 14].

**The fourth issue:** His saying: ﴿And the neighbor who is near, and the neighbor who is far﴾. As for the neighbor, Allah the Exalted commanded guarding him, fulfilling his right, and enjoining the protection of his covenant, in His Book and through the tongue of His Prophet. Do you not see that He, glory be to Him, emphasized his mention after parents and kin, saying: (And the near neighbor), meaning the nearby one.

(And the far neighbor) meaning the stranger. Ibn ʿAbbas said this, and it is also the linguistic meaning. From it comes "so-and-so is *ajnabi*" (foreign), and likewise *al-janabah* means distance. The lexicographers recited:

*"So do not deprive me of a gift from distance,*
*for I am a man, a stranger among the tents."*
[The verse is by ʿAlqamah ibn ʿAbadah, addressing al-Harith ibn Jabalah, praising him. He had captured his brother Shas. By "the gift" he meant freeing his brother Shas from prison, and he freed him and those captured with him from Banu Tamim. (From *al-Lisan*).]

And al-Aʿsha said:

*"I came to Hurayth as a visitor from a distance,*
*and Hurayth was withholding his gift, unyielding."*
[Thus in (z) and in the Diwan of al-Aʿsha, ed. Oppenheimer?, p. 49; and in Tafsir al-Tabari: "Hurayth was striving against my gift"; and in the rest of the originals: "from my gift, praising."]

Al-Aʿmash and al-Mufaddal read (*wal-jari al-junbi*) with a *fatha* on the *jim* and a sukun on the *nun*, and they are two dialects. It is said: *janaba*, *januba*, and *ajnaba*, and *ajnabi*, when there is no kinship between them. Its plural is *ajanib*. It was also said, on the assumption of an omitted genitive: "and the neighbor of the side," meaning the one on the side, i.e., the one from the other direction. Nawf al-Shami said: "The near neighbor" is the Muslim, and "the far neighbor" is the Jew and the Christian.

I say: On this basis, the charge concerning the neighbor is commanded and recommended, whether he is a Muslim or a disbeliever, and this is the correct view. *Ihsan* may mean giving support, and it may mean good companionship, restraining harm, and protecting, which is less than that.

Al-Bukhari narrated from ʿAʾishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Jibril kept enjoining me about the neighbor until I thought he would make him an heir."

It is narrated from Abu Shurayh that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who?" He said: "The one whose neighbor is not safe from his harms." This is general for every neighbor. The Prophet (ﷺ) emphasized abandoning harming him by swearing three times, and that one does not have complete faith if he harms his neighbor. So it is fitting for the believer to beware of harming his neighbor, to refrain from what Allah and His Messenger forbade, and to seek what they approved, urging the servants toward it.

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Neighbors are three: a neighbor who has three rights, a neighbor who has two rights, and a neighbor who has one right. As for the neighbor who has three rights: the Muslim relative neighbor has the right of neighborhood, the right of kinship, and the right of Islam. The neighbor who has two rights is the Muslim neighbor, who has the right of Islam and the right of neighborhood. The neighbor who has one right is the disbeliever, who has the right of neighborhood."

**The fifth issue:** Al-Bukhari narrated from ʿAʾishah, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have two neighbors; to which of them should I give a gift?" He said: "To the nearer of them to you by door." A group of scholars held that this Hadith explains the meaning of His saying: (And the near neighbor), and that it is the one nearest in dwelling to you.

(And the neighbour who is distant)* is the one whose dwelling is far from yours. They used this verse as evidence for making shuf'ah (the right of pre-emption) binding for the neighbour, and they reinforced it with his saying, peace be upon him: "The neighbour has more right to his ṣaqab [[al-ṣaqab: adjacency and nearness, and what is meant by it is shuf'ah.]]." But there is no proof in this. ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, only asked the Prophet ﷺ about whom she should begin with among her neighbours in giving gifts, and he informed her that whoever's door is nearest is more entitled to it than others. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This hadith indicates that the word "neighbour" applies to one who is not adjacent. Abu Hanifa departed from the apparent meaning of this hadith and said: If the adjacent neighbour renounces the shuf'ah, and the one next to him claims it, and there is no shared wall or path to the house, then there is no shuf'ah for him. The majority of scholars say: If a man bequeaths something to his neighbours, both the adjacent and the others receive it, except Abu Hanifa, who differed from the majority of scholars and said: Only the adjacent neighbour alone receives it.

Sixth: People differed concerning the limit of neighbourhood. Al-Awza'i used to say: forty houses in every direction. Ibn Shihab [said something similar]. It is narrated that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have settled in the quarter of a people, and the nearest of them to me in neighbourliness is the one who is most harmful to me." So the Prophet ﷺ sent Abu Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿAli to call out at the doors of the mosques: "Beware! Forty houses constitute a neighbourhood, and whoever's neighbour does not feel safe from his calamities will not enter Paradise." ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: Whoever hears the call (to prayer) is a neighbour. One group said: Whoever hears the iqamah (the call to establish the prayer) is a neighbour of that mosque. Another group said: Whoever dwells with a man in a quarter or a city is his neighbour. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist…﴾ up to His saying ﴿…then they will not be your neighbours in it except for a little.﴾ So He made their gathering in Madinah a form of neighbourliness (jiwar). Neighbourliness has degrees, some closer than others, and the lowest of them is the wife, as the poet said:

"O my neighbour, go away, for you are divorced."
[[This is the first half of a verse by al-A'sha, whose second half is: "Thus are the affairs of people: morning and evening visitors."]]

Seventh: Among the honouring of the neighbour is what Muslim narrated from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Dharr, when you cook a broth, add plenty of water to it and look after your neighbours." He, peace be upon him, thus urged good moral conduct, because of the affection, good companionship and removal of need and harm that it brings about. The neighbour may be harmed by the smell of his neighbour's cooking pot [[al-qatar (with a dammah on the qaf): the smell of the pot, roasted meat, and the like.]], and perhaps he has children, so among the weak of them desire is aroused, and the pain and burden become great for the one responsible for them, especially if that person is weak or a widow, so the hardship grows and the pain and grief intensify for them. It is said that this was the punishment of Ya'qub (Jacob) for his separation from Yusuf (Joseph), peace be upon them both. All of this is removed by sharing with them some of the cooked food that is sent to them. For this reason he, peace be upon him, urged that a near neighbour be given a gift, because he watches what enters his neighbour's house and what leaves it; when he sees that, he wishes to share in it. Also, he is quicker to respond to his neighbour when the neighbour has a need in times of heedlessness and unawareness. Therefore he began with him over the one who is beyond his door even if that person's house is closer. And Allah knows best.

Eighth: The scholars said: When he, peace be upon him, said "add plenty of water to it," he subtly drew attention to making things easy for the stingy person, and he made the increase in something that has no price, namely water. For this reason he did not say, "When you cook a broth, add plenty of its meat," since that would not be easy for everyone. The poet spoke well:

"My pot and my neighbour's pot are one,
and before me it is to him that the pot is lifted."

And he should not give only a small, despised gift, due to the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "Then look for households among your neighbours and give them some of it with *ma'ruf*," meaning with something that is customarily given as a gift. Even a small amount may be given, but it may not fall into the right place. So if only a little is available, let him give it and not belittle it. The recipient must also accept it, due to the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "O women of the believers, let none of you belittle her gift to her neighbour, even if it is the trotter of a sheep, burnt [[al-kura' (trotter): from cattle and sheep, equivalent to the *wazif* of horses, camels and donkeys, the thin part of the leg that is bare of flesh. It is masculine or feminine, and its plural is *akra'* and then *akara'*.]]." Narrated by Malik in his *Muwatta'*.

We have also read *"Ya nisa' al-mu'minat"* in the nominative, not in the construct form. The implied phrase is *ya ayyuha al-nisa' al-mu'minat*, as you say *ya rijal al-kiram*. So the vocative particle is omitted, which is *ya ayyuha*; *al-nisa'* is in implied apposition to *ayyuha*, and *al-mu'minat* is an adjective of *al-nisa'*. It has also been said that it is *ya nisa'a al-mu'minat* in the construct form, but the first reading is more common.

The ninth matter: Among the honouring of the neighbour is that he should not be prevented from driving a piece of wood into his wall, as an act of kindness towards him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "None of you should prevent his neighbour from driving a piece of wood into his wall." Then Abu Hurayrah said: "What is wrong with you that I see you turning away from it? By Allah, I will surely strike it among your shoulders." It is narrated as *khushubahu* and *khashabatan*, in the plural and the singular. It is also narrated as *aktafahum* with a *ta'* and *aknafahum* with a *nun*. The meaning of "I will surely strike it" is: with the saying and the story.

Is this judged as obligatory or recommended? There is a difference among the scholars. Malik, Abu Hanifah and their companions held that its meaning is a recommendation to be good to the neighbour, to overlook his faults and to be kind to him, and that it is not obligatory, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "The property of a Muslim man is not lawful except with the good pleasure of his soul." They said: The meaning of his saying "None of you should prevent his neighbour" is like the meaning of his saying (peace be upon him): "If your wife asks your permission to go to the mosque, let him not prevent her." This, according to all of them, is a recommendation, in accordance with what a man sees as righteous and good in that matter. Al-Shafi'i, his companions, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Dawud ibn Ali and the body of the people of hadith held that this is obligatory. They said: Had Abu Hurayrah not understood from what he heard from the Prophet (peace be upon him) the meaning of obligation, he would not have made obligatory upon them what is not obligatory. This is also the view of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), for he ruled against Muhammad ibn Maslamah in favour of al-Dahhak ibn Khalifah concerning the canal, that it should pass through the land of Muhammad ibn Maslamah. Muhammad ibn Maslamah said: "No, by Allah." Umar said: "By Allah, it shall pass through it, even if it is over your belly." So Umar commanded him to let it pass, and al-Dahhak did so. Malik narrated it in the *Muwatta'*.

Al-Shafi'i claimed in the book *al-Radd* that Malik did not narrate from any of the Companions anything contrary to Umar in this matter. He denied that Malik had narrated it and included it in his book without acting upon it, and he rejected it by his own opinion. Abu Umar said: It is not as al-Shafi'i claimed, because Muhammad ibn Maslamah's opinion in this matter was contrary to Umar's opinion, and the opinion of the Ansar was also contrary to Umar's opinion, as was that of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf in the story of the *rabi'* [[See the *Muwatta'*, chapter "The judgment concerning utilities" (al-marafiq).]] and its diversion. The *rabi'* is the water-wheel. When the Companions differ, reflection must be resorted to, and reflection shows that the blood, property and honour of Muslims are unlawful to one another, except what the soul willingly gives. This is what is established from the Prophet (peace be upon him). The disagreement on this matter is shown by Abu Hurayrah's saying: "What is wrong with you that I see you turning away from it? By Allah, I will surely strike you with it," or something like this.

The first group answered: The judgment concerning utilities is an exception by the Sunnah to the meaning of his saying (peace be upon him): "The property of a Muslim man is not lawful except with the good pleasure of his soul," because that meaning is about ownership and consumption, and utilities are not of that kind, since the Prophet (peace be upon him) distinguished between them in ruling. It is not necessary to combine what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) distinguished. Malik reported that in Medina there was a judge who ruled by this, called Abu al-Mutallib [[In the originals: "called al-Mutallib", and the correction is from the commentary on the *Muwatta'*.]].

As for the reports, they relied on the hadith of al-A'mash from Anas, who said: One of our boys was martyred at the Battle of Uhud, and his mother began wiping the dust from his face and saying: "Rejoice, for Paradise is yours, happily." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to her: "How do you know? Perhaps he used to speak about what did not concern him and withheld what did not harm him." Al-A'mash did not have a valid hearing from Anas, and Allah knows best. Abu Umar said this.

The tenth matter: A hadith has come in which the Prophet (peace be upon him) gathered the rights of the neighbour. It is the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of the neighbour?" He said: "If he asks you for a loan, lend to him; if he seeks your help, help him; if he is in need, give to him; if he is ill, visit him; if he dies, follow his funeral; if good befalls him, let it gladden you and congratulate him; if misfortune befalls him, let it sadden you and console him. Do not harm him with the smoke of your pot, unless you give him some of it. Do not raise your building above him to overlook him and block the wind from him, except with his permission. If you buy fruit, give him some of it; otherwise bring it in secretly, and let none of your children go out with any of it to provoke his children. Do you understand what I say to you? None will fulfil the right of the neighbour except the few whom Allah has mercied." Or a word similar to this. This is a comprehensive hadith and is a good hadith, but in its chain is Abu al-Fadl Uthman ibn Mathar al-Shaybani, who is not reliable.

The eleventh matter: The scholars said: The hadiths on honouring the neighbour came in absolute form, not restricted, even to the disbeliever, as we have explained. In a report they said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we feed them from the meat of the sacrifices?" He said: "Do not feed the polytheists from the sacrifices of the Muslims." His prohibition (peace be upon him) of feeding the polytheists from the sacrifices of the Muslims may refer to the obligatory sacrifice owed upon the one performing it, from which the one performing the rite may not eat, nor feed the rich. As for what is not obligatory, whose feeding of the rich is sufficient, it is permissible to feed the People of the Covenant (*ahl al-dhimmah*) from it. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to Aisha when distributing the meat of the sacrifice: "Begin with our Jewish neighbour." It is also reported that a sheep was slaughtered in the household of Abdullah ibn Amr, and when he came he said: "Did you send a gift to our Jewish neighbour?" three times. "I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'Gabriel kept recommending the neighbour to me, until I thought he would make him an heir.'"

The twelfth matter: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the companion by your side﴾, meaning the fellow traveller. Al-Tabari reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was with a man of his Companions, and they were on two riding beasts. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) entered a thicket [[*Ghaydah* (with a fatha): a thicket, a gathering of trees in the place where water collects.]], and cut two branches, one of them crooked. He came out and gave his companion the straight one. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had more right to this!" He said: "No, O so-and-so. Every companion who accompanies another is answerable for his companionship, even for an hour of a day." Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman said: "Travel has its courtesy, and residence has its courtesy. The courtesy of travel is giving provisions, few disputes with companions, and much good humour in what does not displease Allah. The courtesy of residence is frequenting the mosques, reciting the Qur'an, and many brothers for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

It is attributed to a man of the Banu Asad, and it is said that it belongs to Hatim al-Ta'i:

If my companion does not have, behind my camel,
a mount of his own, as a favour, then may my legs not carry me.
And if he does not have from my provisions a half of my saddlebag,
then may I not be a man of provisions, nor a man of favour.
We are partners in what we are in, and I see
that I owe him a favour for what he has gained of my favour.

Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abi Layla said: "the companion at the side" (al-sahib bi'l-janb) is the wife. Ibn Jurayj said: it is the one who accompanies you and stays with you, hoping for your benefit. The first view is more sound, and it is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid and al-Dahhak. The verse may encompass all of them by its generality. And Allah knows best.

The thirteenth issue: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and the wayfarer﴾. Mujahid said: he is the one who passes by you in transit. The sabil (way) is the road, so the traveller is named after it because he passes along it and keeps to it. Among the kindness owed to him is giving to him, showing him consideration, guiding him and directing him to the right course.

The fourteenth issue: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and what your right hands possess﴾. Allah commanded kindness to the slaves (mamalik), and the Prophet ﷺ explained this. Muslim and others related from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, who said: "We passed by Abu Dharr at al-Rabadhah [[al-Rabadhah (with a vowel on the first letter): a village of Madinah three miles away, where Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him, is buried.]], and he was wearing a cloak, and his slave was wearing the same. We said: 'O Abu Dharr, if you had put the two together it would have been a suit.' He said: 'There was a dispute between me and a man from my brethren, and his mother was a non-Arab, so I reproached him about his mother. He complained about me to the Prophet ﷺ, and I met the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: (O Abu Dharr, you are a man in whom there is still jahiliyyah.) I said: O Messenger of Allah, do those who revile men revile his father and mother? He said: (O Abu Dharr, you are a man in whom there is still jahiliyyah. They are your brothers, whom Allah has placed under your authority. So feed them from what you eat, clothe them from what you wear, do not burden them with what overwhelms them, and if you burden them, then help them.)'" It is related from Abu Hurayrah that he once rode a mule and seated his slave behind him, and someone said to him: "If only you had let him dismount and run behind your animal." Abu Hurayrah said: "For two bundles of fire to burn before me what they have burned is dearer to me than that my slave should run behind me." Abu Dawud related from Abu Dharr who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Whoever among your slaves is compatible with you, feed him from what you eat and clothe him from what you clothe yourselves; and whoever among them is not compatible with you, sell him, and do not torment the creation of Allah.) Compatible (la'amakum) means agreeable to you, and mula'amah means agreement. Muslim related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (The slave has his food and his clothing, and he is not burdened with work beyond what he can bear.) He, peace be upon him, also said: (None of you should say "my slave" or "my slave-girl"; rather let him say "my young man" and "my young woman".) Its explanation will come in Surat Yusuf, peace be upon him [[See vol. 9, pp. 176, 188, 222.]]. The Prophet ﷺ thus urged masters towards noble character, encouraged them to it, and guided them to kindness and to the path of humility, so that they would not see themselves as superior to their slaves, since all are slaves of Allah and all wealth is Allah's wealth. But He subjected some of them to others and made some of them owners of others, to complete His blessing and carry out His wisdom. If they feed them less than they eat, or clothe them less than they wear, in kind or in quantity, it is permissible, provided he fulfils his obligation towards them. There is no disagreement on this, and Allah knows best. Muslim related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr that a qahraman (steward) of his came to him, entered and said: "Have you given the slaves their sustenance?" He said: "No." He said: "Go and give it to them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (It is sin enough for a man to withhold the sustenance of those whom he owns.) [[Al-qahraman (with the qaf vowelled as fatha or damma): like a treasurer, agent and guardian, one who is in charge of what is under his hand and who manages a man's affairs, a Persian term.]]

The fifteenth issue: It is established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: (Whoever strikes his slave with a prescribed punishment when it was not due, or slaps him, his expiation is to free him.) [[The hadith in Muslim: (He struck a boy of his...) then the expiation.]] Its meaning is that he struck him an amount equal to a prescribed punishment when no prescribed punishment was due to him. It has come from a group of the Companions that they applied retaliation (qisas) against a son for striking a servant, and they freed the servant when the retaliation was not wanted. The Prophet ﷺ also said: (Whoever falsely accuses his slave of fornication, Allah will impose upon him the prescribed punishment on the Day of Resurrection, eighty lashes.) He, peace be upon him, also said: (One who treats his slaves badly will not enter Paradise [[i.e. one who mistreats those he owns.]].) He, peace be upon him, also said: (Bad character is ill omen, and good treatment of slaves is growth, and keeping the ties of kinship increases lifespan, and charity averts a bad death.)

The sixteenth issue: The scholars differed on this topic as to which is better, the free man or the slave. Muslim related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The righteous slave has two rewards.) And by Him in whose hand is the soul of Abu Hurayrah, were it not for jihad in the way of Allah, the Hajj and dutifulness to my mother, I would love to die while being a slave. It is related from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (If the slave sincerely advises his master and worships Allah well, he has his reward twice.) From this and similar reports, the excellence of the slave is derived, because he is addressed from two directions: he is required to worship Allah and required to serve his master. This is the view of Abu 'Umar Yusuf ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari and Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-'Amiri al-Baghdadi al-Hafiz. Those who prefer the free man argued: independence in the affairs of religion and of the world is achieved only by free people, and the slave is like one who is absent for lack of independence, like a tool directed by force, and like a beast subjected by compulsion. For this reason he is deprived of positions of testimony and most offices of authority, and his prescribed limits are less than those of free people, as an indication of the lowliness of his rank. The free man, even if he is required in one respect only, has more duties in it and greater burden, so his reward is greater. Abu Hurayrah alluded to this with his saying: "Were it not for jihad and the Hajj," meaning were it not for the deficiency that befalls the slave through missing these matters. And Allah knows best.

The seventeenth issue: Anas ibn Malik related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: (Jibril kept enjoining me concerning the neighbour until I thought he would make him an heir. He kept enjoining me concerning women until I thought he would make their divorce unlawful. He kept enjoining me concerning slaves until I thought he would set a term for them, when they reach it they would be freed. He kept enjoining me concerning the siwak until I feared it would wear away my mouth [[another narration: until it nearly did]]. He kept enjoining me concerning qiyam al-layl until I thought that the best of my Ummah would not sleep at night.) Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi mentioned it in his tafsir.

The eighteenth issue: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed Allah does not love﴾, meaning does not approve. ﴿one who is self-deluded and boastful﴾. He, Glorified is He, negated His love and approval for one who has this attribute, meaning that the signs of His blessings will not appear upon him in the Hereafter. In this there is a kind of warning. The mukhtal is the one possessed of arrogance (khuyala), that is pride. The fakhur is one who counts his virtues out of pride. Fakhr is boasting and haughtiness [[In ṭ: praise.]]. These two attributes were specifically mentioned here because they lead their possessors to disdain the near poor, the neighbour who is poor, and others mentioned in the verse, so that Allah's command to be kind to them is neglected. 'Asim, as reported by al-Mufaddal from him, read "wal-jar al-janb" with a fatha on the jim and sukun on the nun. Al-Mahdawi said: it is on the assumption of an elided mudaf, meaning "wal-jar dhi al-janb", that is, the neighbour who is in a side, i.e. remote. Al-Akhfash recited:
"The people are a side, and the amir is a side" [[as if he equated the whole of the people with him.]]
And al-janb is the side, i.e. one who keeps away from kin. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 37:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon people﴾. On this there are two issues.

The first: His words, exalted is He, ﴿Those who are stingy﴾. (Alladhina) is in the accusative position as a substitute (badal) for (man) in His words (man kana), and it cannot be an adjective (sifah), because (man) and (ma) are not described and cannot be used to describe. It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative position as a substitute for the pronoun in (fakhur). It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative position, so that it is conjoined to it [[i.e., His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾, as in I'rab al-Quran by al-Nahhas.]]. It is also permissible for it to be a new subject (mubtada') with the predicate omitted, meaning "Those who are stingy, for them is such-and-such," or the predicate is (Indeed Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom). It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning "I mean," so the verse is about the believers, and according to this interpretation the verse conveys that love of Allah is negated from those who are stingy, so be good, O believers, to those who are named, for Allah does not love whoever has the traits that prevent generosity.

The second: His words, exalted is He, ﴿They are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon people﴾. Stinginess that is blameworthy in the Shari'ah (bukhl) is refraining from paying what Allah, exalted is He, has made obligatory upon a person. This is like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And let not those who are stingy with what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them﴾, the verse. The discussion of stinginess, its reality, and the distinction between it and miserliness (shuhh) has already been covered fully in (Al 'Imran) [[See vol. 4, p. 290.]]. According to the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and others, the intended people in this verse are the Jews, for they combined arrogance, boastfulness, stinginess with wealth, and concealing what Allah revealed in the Torah concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: the intended are the hypocrites, whose spending and faith were out of dissimulation (taqiyyah). The meaning is: Indeed Allah does not love every arrogant boaster, nor those who are stingy, according to the parsing we have mentioned.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾. He, exalted is He, distinguished the threat against the stingy believers from the threat against the disbelievers, by making the first the absence of love and the second a humiliating punishment.

**Second issue:** Concerning His words, ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾ to the end of the verse. God joined this to "those who are stingy" (*alladhina yabkhaluna*): "those who spend their wealth to be seen by people." It is also said that it is a conjunction with "the disbelievers," so it would be in the genitive position (*fi mawdi' khafd*). Whoever holds that the *waw* is extra (*ziyadat al-waw*) permits that the second element be the predicate (*khabar*) of the first. The majority said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because of His words, "to be seen by people." Showing off (*riya'*) is one of the forms of hypocrisy (*nifaq*). Mujahid said it was about the Jews. Al-Tabari weakened this view, because God negated from this category (*sinf*)[[The *sinf* (with a kasra on the sad and a sukun on the nun) is a group from a tribe. It is also said to be a group from any thing.]] faith in God and the Last Day, and the Jews are not like that. Ibn 'Atiyya said: Mujahid's view is sound as hyperbole and as a binding argument, since their belief in the Last Day is as if there were no belief, in that it does not benefit them. It is also said: it was revealed concerning the feeders of Badr, who were the leaders of Mecca; they spent on the people so that they would go out to Badr. Ibn al-'Arabi said: spending for show (*nafaqat al-riya'*) enters the rulings in that it is not valid. I say: the following words of God point to this in the Book: ﴿Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you﴾. It will come (*wa sa-ya'ti*).[[See vol. 8, p. 161.]]

**Third issue:** Concerning His words, ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is the companion﴾. There is an implied element in the speech; its estimate is: "and they do not believe in God or in the Last Day." So their companion is Satan. (*wa man yakun al-shaytanu lahu qarinan fa-sa'a qarinan*). The *qarin* is the one who accompanies, that is, the companion and the close friend. It is a *fa'il* form from *iqran* (joining). 'Adi ibn Zayd said:

*Do not ask about a man, but ask about his companion,*
*for every companion is guided by his fellow.*[[In b, j, z, and t: "fa-inna al-qarin." In d and t: "wa-absar qarinahu," which is a variant. This verse is also narrated for Tarafa.]]

The meaning is: whoever accepts from Satan in this world has become his companion. It is also permitted that the meaning is: whoever is joined with Satan in the Fire, (*fa-sa'a qarinan*), that is, "then evil is Satan as a companion," and *qarinan* is in the accusative of specification (*tamyiz*).

(مَا) is in the nominative position as the subject (mubtada', the subject of a nominal sentence), and (ذَا) is its predicate (khabar, the predicate). ذَا here has the sense of الَّذِي (alladhi, "which" or "who"). It is also permissible for مَا وَذَا to be a single noun. On the first reading, its implied form is "وَمَا الَّذِي عَلَيْهِمْ" ("and what is it that is upon them"). On the second, its implied form is "وَأَيُّ شي عَلَيْهِمْ" ("and what thing is upon them").

(﴿If they had believed in Allah and the Last Day﴾), meaning: they would have affirmed the Necessarily Existent (wājib al-wujūd), and what the Messenger brought of the details of the Hereafter. (﴿And spent from what Allah has provided them﴾).

(﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of them﴾). Its meaning has been explained previously in other places.

**Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 4, verse 40:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (anyone) the weight of an atom﴾, meaning He does not diminish for them, nor reduce from the reward of their deeds, even the weight of an atom. Rather, He repays them for it and rewards them for it. The meaning of the statement is that Allah, Exalted is He, does not wrong anyone, whether a little or a lot, as He said, Exalted is He: (Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all) [[See vol. 8, p. 346.]]. The *dharrah* (atom) is the red ant, according to Ibn Abbas and others, and it is the smallest of ants. It is also related from him that it is the head of an ant. Yazid ibn Harun said: "They claim that the atom has no weight." It is related that a man placed some bread and the ants covered it to the extent that they concealed it, then he weighed it, and it added nothing to the weight of the bread. I say: The Qur'an and the Sunnah indicate that the atom has weight, just as the dinar and half a dinar have weight. And Allah knows best. It has also been said that the *dharrah* is the mustard seed, as He said, Exalted is He: (So no soul will be wronged at all, and even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth) [[See vol. 11, p. 293.]]. Other views have been mentioned, but in general it is an expression for the smallest and least of things. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong a believer a good deed; he is given for it in this world and rewarded for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for the good deeds he did for Allah in this world, until when he reaches the Hereafter he has no good deed for which he is rewarded."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾, meaning He increases its reward. The people of the Hijaz read *hasanatun* (a good deed) with a *raf'* (nominative ending), while the majority read it with a *nasb* (accusative ending).
