Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 113:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾

What follows "lawla" (لَوْلا, "were it not for")

It is in the nominative case by being the subject of a nominal clause (mubtada'), according to Sibawayh, and its predicate (khabar) is omitted and not expressed. The meaning is: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾

by His alerting you to the truth. It was also said: by prophethood and protection from error (al-'isma).

﴿A group among them would have resolved to mislead you﴾

from the truth, because they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to clear Ibn Ubayriq of the accusation and to attribute it to the Jew. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed His favour upon His Messenger, peace be upon him, by alerting him to that and informing him of it.

﴿But they mislead only themselves﴾

because they act in the manner of those who go astray, so its harm returns upon them.

﴿And they cannot harm you in anything﴾

because you are protected (ma'sum).

﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾

This is the beginning of a new statement. It was also said: the waw is for the circumstantial (hal), like your saying: "I came to you while the sun was rising." From it is the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

"And I set out early while the birds are in their nests"

So the speech is connected, meaning: they cannot harm you in anything along with Allah's sending down the Qur'an to you.

﴿And wisdom﴾

The judgment by revelation.

﴿And taught you what you did not know﴾

That is, of the laws and rulings. And (تَعْلَمُ, "you knew") is in the accusative position, because it is the predicate of kana (كان). The damma was dropped from the nun for the jussive, and the waw was dropped due to the meeting of two sukun.

He means the scheming that the people of Banu Ubayriq discussed among themselves and then mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ). *Al-najwa* means a private conversation between two people. One says *nājaytu fulānan munājāة wa-najāʾan* ("I conferred privately with so-and-so"), and *hum yantajūna* and *yatanājawna* ("they confer privately"). One also says *najawtu fulānan anjūhu najwan*, meaning "I conferred privately with him." So *najwā* is derived from *najawtu al-shayʾa anjūhu*, meaning "I separated and isolated the thing." *Al-najwah* is a raised piece of ground, so called because it stands apart by being higher than what surrounds it. The poet says:

*Whoever is in his elevated place is like whoever is in his courtyard,*
*and the one who stays hidden is like one who walks in the open with nothing above him.*

[[The verse is by Aws ibn Ḥajar, though it is also attributed to ʿUbayd. *Al-ʿaqwa* is the open yard and the area around a house and its quarter. *Al-qirwāḥ* is something exposed, with nothing above it to shelter it from the sky. A marginal note in one manuscript says: a tall she-camel, and likewise a tall palm tree, is called *qirwāḥ*.]]

So *al-najwā* is a verbal noun meaning private discourse, and it may also be used for the group that confers privately, as one says *qawmun ʿadlun* and *riḍan* (a people who are just and acceptable). God the Exalted says: ﴿when they hold secret counsel﴾. On the first reading, the matter is an exception from a different category, which is the discontinuous exception (*al-istithnāʾ al-munqaṭiʿ*), and this has already been discussed. In that case *man* (in the phrase ﴿except for one who enjoins charity﴾) is in the nominative position, meaning: "But whoever enjoins charity, or what is good, or reconciliation between people, and calls to it, there is good in his private discourse." *Man* may also be in the genitive position, and the sense would then be: "There is no good in much of their private talk, except the private talk of one who enjoins charity," with the rest omitted. On the second reading, where *al-najwā* is a name for the group of those conferring privately, *man* is in the genitive position as a substitute (*badal*), meaning: "There is no good in much of their private talk, except in one who enjoins charity." Or it may be in the accusative position, according to the one who says: "I passed by no one except Zayd."

Some commentators, including al-Zajjāj, said: *al-najwā* is the speech of a group that holds private talk, or of two people, whether it is secret or spoken aloud. But this is far-fetched. And God knows best.

*Al-maʿrūf* is a term that covers all acts of righteousness. Muqātil said: *al-maʿrūf* here means the obligatory duty (*al-farḍ*), but the first view is more correct.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every act of good is charity, and among good acts is that you meet your brother with a cheerful face." The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "Good is according to its name, and the first to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection are good and its people."

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may God be pleased with him) said: "Let not the ingratitude of one who is ungrateful for good deter you from doing good, for a grateful person may give thanks many times over the denial of the unbeliever."

Al-Ḥuṭayʾah said:

*Whoever does good will not lack those who repay it;*
*good deeds are not lost between God and people.*

[[In all the manuscripts it is *jawāʾizuhu* ("his rewards"), not *jawāzihu*.]]

Al-Riyāshī recited:

*The hand that does good is a gain wherever it is,*
*whether a thankless one or a thankful one carries it.*

*So in the thanks of the thankful one for it there is a reward,*
*and with God is what the ungrateful one has denied.*

Al-Māwardī said: "Whoever is able to do good should hasten to do it, fearing that the opportunity will pass, and rush to it, fearing his own inability. He should know that it is one of the opportunities of his time and one of the spoils of what is possible for him. He should not neglect it out of confidence in his ability to do it later. How many a confident person has seen his ability slip away, leaving him regret, and how many a person who relied on power has seen it vanish, leaving him shame. As the poet said:

*I kept hearing how many a confident person was shamed,*
*until I was tested and became the confident one who was shamed.*

If a person were alert to the calamities of his time and guarded against the consequences of his affairs, his gains would be stored up and his losses would be made good. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: 'Whoever has a door of good opened to him should seize it, for he does not know when it will be closed to him.'" It is also related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "Everything has a fruit, and the fruit of good is haste (*al-sarāḥ*)." [[*Al-sarāḥ* means hastening.]]

It was said to Anushirvan: "What are the greatest calamities for you?" He said: "That you are able to do good but do not do it until the opportunity has passed."

ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd said: "Whoever delays an opportunity beyond its time should be certain of losing it."

One of the poets said:

*When your winds blow, seize them,*
*for every stormy gust has a calm.*

*Do not neglect kindness in it,*
*for you do not know when the calm will come.*

One of the people of dignity wrote to a governor who had neglected to honour his dignity:

*Do you intend to be on the path of honouring my dignity,*
*or do you grant favours only in the reckoning?*

*I want you, for the benefit of this world, so awaken*
*to my needs from the sleep of the sleepers.*

Al-ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with him) said: "Good is not complete except with three qualities: hastening it, minimising it, and concealing it. When you hasten it, you bring it joy; when you minimise it, you magnify it; and when you conceal it, you complete it."

One of the poets said:

*Your good deed has grown greater in my estimation,*
*that it is hidden with you and small.*

*You forget it as if you had never done it,*
*yet among the people it is famous and great.*

Among the conditions of doing good is leaving off reminding others of it and leaving off self-admiration at having done it, because both of these cancel gratitude and nullify the reward. This has already been explained in al-Baqarah. [[See vol. 3, p. 311.]]

God's statement ﴿or reconciliation between people﴾ is general. It applies to bloodshed, property, and honour, and to every matter over which Muslims quarrel and disagree, and to every speech that is intended for the sake of God the Exalted. In a report: "All of a son of Adam's speech is against him, not for him, except what is an enjoining of good, a forbidding of evil, or a remembrance of God the Exalted." As for one who seeks display and leadership, he will not attain the reward. ʿUmar wrote to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may God be pleased with him): "Send back the disputants until they reconcile, for the giving of judgement produces enmity between them."

What is forbidden of private discourse and what is permitted will come later in al-Mujādilah, God willing. [[See vol. 17, p. 294 onward.]]

It is related from Anas ibn Mālik (may God be pleased with him) that he said: "Whoever reconciles two people, God will grant him for every word the freeing of a slave." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abū Ayyūb: "Shall I not direct you to a charity that God and His Messenger love? It is that you reconcile people when they have fallen into corruption, and bring them close when they have drawn apart." Al-Awzāʿī said: "No step is more beloved to God the Mighty and Majestic than a step taken to reconcile people. Whoever reconciles two people, God will record for him an immunity from the Fire." Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir said: "Two men disputed in a corner of the mosque, so I went over to them and kept at them until they reconciled. Abū Hurayrah, who was watching me, said: 'I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: whoever reconciles two people earns the reward of a martyr.'"

Abū Muṭīʿ Makḥūl ibn al-Mufaḍḍal al-Nasafī mentioned these reports in his book *al-Lu'lu'iyyāt*. I found it in the author's handwriting on a sheet, and he did not note where it was from (may God be pleased with him).

*Ibtighāʾ* (in the verse ﴿seeking the pleasure of God﴾) is in the accusative as an object of purpose (*al-mafʿūl li-ajlihi*).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on Surah 4, verses 115–116:

There are two issues here.

**The first issue:** The scholars said: These two verses were revealed concerning Ibn Ubayriq the thief, when the Prophet (ﷺ) [upon him] ruled that his hand be cut off. He fled to Mecca and apostatized. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When he reached Mecca, he broke into a house there, and the polytheists caught him and killed him. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ up to His saying: ﴿he has certainly strayed far astray﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: A group of the Quraysh came to Medina and embraced Islam, then they returned to Mecca as apostates, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾. *Al-mushaqqah* (opposition) means enmity.

Even though the verse was revealed concerning the thief of the armor or someone else, it is general in application to everyone who opposes the path of the Muslims. *Al-huda* (guidance) means right direction and clarification, and this has been discussed previously [See vol. 1, p. 160].

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We will leave him to what he has turned to﴾, it is said that it was revealed concerning those who apostatized. The meaning is: We will leave him with what he worships. This is related from Mujahid, meaning: We will entrust him to the idols which neither benefit nor harm. Muqatil also said this.

Al-Kalbi said: The saying of the Exalted, ﴿We will leave him to what he has turned to﴾, was revealed concerning Ibn Ubayriq. When his condition and his theft became apparent, he fled to Mecca and apostatized, and he broke into a wall belonging to a man in Mecca called Hajjaj ibn 'Ilat. He fell and remained in the breach until he was found in that state. They expelled him from Mecca, so he went out to Syria and stole some of the property of a caravan. They stoned him and killed him. Then it was revealed: ﴿We will leave him to what he has turned to and drive him into Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾.

'Asim, Hamzah and Abu 'Amr read *nuwallihi* and *nuslihi* with the *ha'* vowelless (*bi-jazm al-ha'*), while the rest read it with a kasra, and both are dialectal forms.

**The second issue:** The scholars said, regarding the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, it is evidence for the validity of the position of *ijma'* (scholarly consensus). Regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, it is a refutation of the Khawarij (*al-Khawarij*), who claimed that the perpetrator of a major sin is a disbeliever. This matter has been discussed previously.

Al-Tirmidhi related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: There is no verse in the Qur'an more beloved to me than this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [He said]: This is a *gharib* (rare) hadith.

Ibn Furak said: Our companions (the Ash'aris) agreed that eternal abiding in the Fire is only for the disbeliever, and that the sinner among the people of the *qiblah* (Muslims), if he dies without repenting, then if he is punished with the Fire, he will inevitably leave it through the intercession of the Messenger, or through the commencement of mercy from Allah the Exalted.

Al-Dahhak said: An old man from the Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I am an old man immersed in sins and transgressions, except that I have not associated anything with Allah since I came to know Him and believed in Him. So what is my state with Allah? Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, the verse.

Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 4, verse 117:

Allah's words: ﴿They call upon, besides Him,﴾ meaning besides Allah, ﴿only females﴾ (إِلَّا إِنَاثًا). It was revealed concerning the people of Makkah, when they worshipped idols. Here "إِنْ" is a negative particle meaning "مَا" (ma, "not"). "إِنَاثًا" means idols, namely al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat. Every tribe had an idol that it worshipped, and they would say: "The female of the such-and-such clan." This is related by al-Hasan and Ibn 'Abbas. With each idol was its devil (shaytan), which appeared to the custodians (sadana, the keepers of the idols) and the soothsayers (kahana, pl. of kahin, diviners) and spoke to them. So the statement came in the form of astonishment, because the female of every kind is its most base. This is ignorance on the part of one who associates with Allah an inanimate object and names it female, or believes it to be female.

It was also said: "إِلَّا إِنَاثًا" means lifeless objects (mawat), because lifeless things have no spirit, such as a piece of wood or a stone. Lifeless things are referred to in the same way as the feminine is referred to, without changing their rank. You say: "The stones please me," just as you say: "The woman pleases me."

It was also said: "إِلَّا إِنَاثًا" means angels, because of their saying: "The angels are the daughters of Allah," and they are our intercessors with Allah. This is related from al-Dahhak.

The reading of Ibn 'Abbas is "إِلَّا وَثَنًا" (except an idol), with a fatha on the waw and the tha, as a singular noun of genus. He also read "وُثُنًا" with a damma on the tha and the waw, the plural of "وَثَنٌ" (wathan, idol). "أَوْثَانٌ" (awthan) is also a plural of "وَثَنٌ," like "أَسَدٌ" and "آسَادٌ." Al-Nahhas said: "He did not read it in this way, as far as I know." I say: Abu Bakr al-Anbari has mentioned: my father told us, Nasr ibn Dawud told us, Abu 'Ubayd told us, Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she used to read: "إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَوْثَانًا" (They call upon, besides Him, only idols).

Ibn 'Abbas also read "إِلَّا أُثُنًا," as if he had made "وَثَنًا" into the plural "وِثَانٌ," just as you say "جَمَلٌ" and "جِمَالٌ" (camel and camels). Then he made "أَوْثَانًا" into the plural "وُثُنٌ," just as you say "مِثَالٌ" and "مُثُلٌ" (example and examples). Then he changed the waw into a hamza because it was preceded by a damma, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And when the messengers are brought to their appointed time﴾ (وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ), from "الْوَقْتِ" (appointed time). So "أُثُنٌ" is the plural of a plural. (See vol. 19, p. 155.)

The Prophet (ﷺ) read "إِلَّا اثْنَا" (only females), the plural of "أَنِيثٌ," like "غَدِيرٌ" and "غُدُرٌ" (pool and pools). Al-Tabari related that it is the plural of "إِنَاثٌ," like "ثِمَارٌ" and "ثُمُرٌ" (fruit and fruits). Abu 'Amr al-Dani related this reading from the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: "It was also read by Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Abu Haywa."

Allah's words: ﴿And they call upon none but a rebellious devil﴾ (وَإِنْ يَدْعُونَ إِلَّا شَيْطَانًا مَرِيدًا). It means Iblis, because when they obey him in what he adorns for them, they have worshipped him. A parallel in meaning is: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ (اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ), meaning they obeyed them in what they commanded them, not that they worshipped them. (See vol. 8, p. 119.) This will come later. The derivation of the word "shaytan" has already been discussed. (See vol. 1, p. 90.)

"Marid" means the stubborn, the rebellious, on the pattern "فَعِيلٌ" from "مَرَدَ," when one becomes insolent. Al-Azhari said: "Marid is one who has gone out of obedience. A man 'yamrudu, murud' when he becomes insolent and departs from obedience, so he is 'marid,' 'marid' and 'mutamarrid.'" Ibn 'Arafa said: "It is one whose evil has become apparent. From this comes the expression 'shajara marda,' a tree whose leaves have fallen so that its branches are visible, and from it is said of a man 'amrad,' meaning the visible part of the cheeks where the hair is."

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 118:

Allah's words, ﴿God cursed him﴾. The root meaning of *al-la'n* (cursing) is distancing [[See vol. 2, p. 25.]]. Customarily it is distancing accompanied by displeasure and anger. Cursing a specific person is permissible: God's curse upon Iblis (Satan) by name is permitted, and likewise upon the dead among the disbelievers, such as Pharaoh (Fir'awn), Haman (Haman), and Abu Jahl. As for the living, the discussion of this has already passed in (al-Baqarah) [[See vol. 2, p. 188.]].

Allah's words, ﴿And he said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾ That is, Satan said. The meaning is: I will surely draw them away through my misguidance and lead them astray through my leading astray. They are the disbelievers and the disobedient. In a report (khabar): "From every thousand, one is for God and the rest are for Satan." I say: This is correct in meaning, and it is supported by Allah's words to Adam on the Day of Resurrection: "Send forth the group for the Fire." He will say: "And what is the group for the Fire?" He will say: "From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine." Related by Muslim. The group for the Fire is the portion of Satan. And Allah knows best.

It was also said: among the "portion" is their obedience to him in matters, including that they would strike a nail for the newborn at its birth, and circle with it on its seventh day, saying: "So that the *ʿumār* (inhabitants of the house) may know him." (*ʿumār al-buyut*: its inhabitants, meaning the jinn who dwell in houses.) In Ibn ʿAtiyya: the word *mafrud* (appointed) in this place means "set apart," from *al-fard*, which is a notch in a stick or the like.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 119 (part 1 of 2):

There are nine issues in this.

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And I will surely lead them astray﴾, meaning I will surely turn them away from the path of guidance.

(And I will surely arouse their desires) meaning I will surely make them fancy [false hopes], from tamannī (wishing). This is not restricted to one kind of desire, because each person is aroused by his own desire according to his inclination and the circumstances of his situation. It has also been said: "And I will surely arouse their desires" means long life, good, repentance, and knowledge together with persistence [in sin].

(And I will surely command them, and they will surely cut off the ears of cattle). Al-batk means cutting. From it comes saif bātik, meaning a cutting sword. I will command them to cut the ears of the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah, and the like. It is said: batakahu and battakahu (lightened and intensified), and fī yadihi bitkah, meaning a piece; the plural is bitak. Zuhayr said [[this is the second half of a line, whose first half is:
ḥattā idhā mā hawat kaff al-ghulām lahā.]]:
ṭārat wa fī kaffihi min rīshihā bitak
("It flew off, and in his hand there remained a piece of its feathers.")

The second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah﴾. The lām-particles here are all for oath.

The scholars differed over what this alteration refers to. One group said: it is castration, the gouging out of eyes, and the cutting of ears. This was the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Anas, ʿIkrimah and Abū Ṣāliḥ.

All of that is torment of animals, and making lawful and unlawful by transgression, and speech without proof or evidence.

Ears in cattle are beauty and benefit, and so are other limbs; for this reason Satan saw fit to alter the creation of Allah, exalted is He, by them.

In the ḥadīth of ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār al-Mujāshiʿī:
("Indeed I created My servants as ḥunafā' (upright), all of them, and indeed the devils came to them and led them astray (ijtālat-hum) from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for, and commanded them to alter My creation.")
[ijtālat-hum: they made them light-minded and they went about with them in error.]
The ḥadīth was transmitted by al-Qāḍī Ismāʿīl, and Muslim also.

Ismāʿīl narrated: he said: Abū al-Walīd and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb told us, both saying: Shuʿbah told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from his father, who said:

I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I was of shabby appearance. He said:
("Do you have any wealth?")
He said: I said: Yes.
He said: ("Of what kind of wealth?")
I said: Of all kinds of wealth: horses, camels, slaves. Abū al-Walīd said: and sheep. He said:
("When Allah has given you wealth, let the sign of it be seen upon you.") Then he said:
("Do you have your camels producing young (tantaj) for your people, sound of ear? Then do you go to a camel and slit its ears, and say, 'This is baḥīrah,' and slit its hide, and say, 'This is ṣurum,' to make them forbidden to you and to your family?")
He said: I said: Yes, indeed.
He said: ("Everything that Allah has given you is lawful. Allah's cutter is sharper than your cutter, and Allah's strength is greater than your strength.")
He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you say of a man whom I stayed with, and he did not host me, then he stayed with me; shall I host him, or repay him?
He said: ("Rather, host him.")

The second issue: Since this was an act and effect of Satan, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us (to examine the eye and the ear [well]) — meaning to consider whether they are free of a defect that may be in them; the defect of the eye is blindness, and the defect of the ear is its being cut — or (it is from al-sharfah, which is the choicest of property, meaning he commanded us to choose them). We should not sacrifice a one-eyed animal, nor one with a cut ear in front (muqābalah), nor one with a cut ear at the back (mudābarah), nor one with a split ear (kharqā'), nor one with a slit ear (sharqā'). Abū Dāwūd transmitted it from ʿAlī, who said: "He commanded us," and mentioned it.

Al-muqābalah: the animal whose tip of the ear is cut.
Al-mudābarah: the animal whose back of the ear is cut.
Al-sharqā': the animal whose ear is split.
Al-kharqā': the animal whose ear is pierced by the brand.
A defect in the ear is taken into account by the majority of scholars.
Mālik and al-Layth said: an animal whose ear is cut off, or most of its ear, is not acceptable; a slit for branding is acceptable. This is also the view of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority of jurists.
If it is sakkāʾ, which is one born without an ear, Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī said: it is not permissible. If it has a small ear, it is acceptable; a similar view is reported from Abū Ḥanīfah.

The fourth issue: As for the castration of animals, a group of scholars permitted it when the benefit is intended, either for fattening or for other purposes.

The majority of scholars and their community hold that there is no harm in sacrificing a castrated animal, and some of them regarded it as commendable if it is fatter than others.

ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz permitted the castration of horses. ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr castrated a mule of his.

Mālik permitted the castration of male sheep. That is permissible because it is not intended as tying the animal to the religion (taʿlīq al-ḥāl bi-l-dīn) for an idol that is worshipped, nor for a Lord who is affirmed as one; rather it is intended to improve the meat that is eaten, and to strengthen the male when his desire for the female has ceased.

Some disliked that, based on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: ("Only those who do not know do that.")
Ibn al-Mundhir chose this view and said: because it is established from Ibn ʿUmar, who used to say: "It is the growth of Allah's creation." ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān also disliked it.

Al-Awzāʿī said: "They used to dislike castrating anything that has offspring."

Ibn al-Mundhir said: On this there are two ḥadīths:
One of them from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ forbade castrating sheep, cattle, camels and horses.
The other is the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet ﷺ forbade ṣabr al-rūḥ (the holding of a living thing and shooting it until it dies) and the castration of animals.

What is in the Muwaṭṭaʾ on this subject is what he mentioned from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he used to dislike castration and would say: "In it is the completion of the creation (tamām al-khalq)."

Abū ʿUmar said: meaning that in not castrating is the completion of creation; and it is also narrated as "the growth of creation (namāʾ al-khalq)."

I say: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Ghanī transmitted it from the ḥadīth of ʿUmar ibn Ismāʿīl, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: ("Do not castrate what increases the creation of Allah.")

Al-Dāraquṭnī's teacher narrated it to him, saying: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Muʿaddil told us [the text reads "al-Muʿaddil" with unmarked dāl; it may be Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muʿadhdhil with a dotted letter] — ʿAbbās ibn Muḥammad told us, Abū Mālik al-Nakhaʿī told us, from ʿUmar ibn Ismāʿīl, and he mentioned it.

Al-Dāraquṭnī said: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn al-Nuʿmān also narrated it from Abū Mālik.

The fifth issue: As for castration of a human being, it is a calamity, for when he is castrated his heart and strength are destroyed, the reverse of an animal, and his offspring, which he was commanded to produce in the saying of the Prophet ﷺ ("Marry and multiply, for I will boast of you before the nations") [in the originals and most books this is the reading; the correct narration, as in al-Bayhaqī, is: "Marry, increase, for I will boast of you among the nations on the Day of Resurrection"; see Kashf al-Khafā' vol. 1 p. 318], is cut off. Furthermore, there is great pain in it which may lead its victim to destruction, so there is waste of property and loss of life, and all of that is forbidden.

Moreover, this is mutilation (muthlah), and the Prophet ﷺ forbade mutilation, and that is authentic.

A group of jurists of the Ḥijāz and Kūfa disliked buying castrated slaves from the Ṣaqāliba and others, and they said: "If they were not bought from them, they would not be castrated."

They did not differ that castrating human beings is not lawful nor permissible, because it is mutilation and alteration of the creation of Allah, exalted is He; and likewise cutting off any of their other limbs without a legal prescription (ḥadd) or retaliation (qawd). Abū ʿUmar said.

The sixth issue: Having established this, know that branding and marking are excepted from his prohibition, peace be upon him, of the "Satan's sign" (sharīṭat al-shayṭān), which is what we have already mentioned of his prohibition of torturing animals with fire. Al-wasm is branding with fire; its root is the mark. It is said: wasama al-shay' yasimuhu, when he marked the thing with a sign by which it is recognized, and from it is His saying: (Their mark is on their faces). Al-sīmā is the sign, and al-mīsam is the branding iron.

In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim it is established from Anas who said:
"I saw in the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the branding iron, and he was branding the camels of the ṣadaqah, the fayʾ and other things, so that every property is recognized and its due is paid, and it is not diverted to anything else."

The seventh issue: Branding is permitted on all limbs except the face, based on what Jābir narrated, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade striking the face and branding the face." Muslim transmitted it.

That was only because of the face's nobility above the limbs, since it is the seat of beauty and loveliness, and because by it the living creature is sustained. The Prophet ﷺ passed by a man beating his slave and said: ("Beware of the face, for Allah created Adam in His image [ʿalā ṣūratih]") — meaning in the image of the one being beaten; that is, the face of this beaten one resembles the face of Adam, so it should be respected because of its resemblance.

This is the best of what has been said in its interpretation, and Allah knows best.

Another group said: the reference of "alteration" is to tattooing and what is similar to it of artificial embellishment for beauty. This was said by Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan.

And among that is the authentic ḥadīth from ʿAbd Allāh who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ("Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and the women who have themselves tattooed, and the women who pluck (the facial hair) and the women who have it done, and the women who file their teeth apart for beauty, who alter the creation of Allah.") [the addition is from Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim] — the ḥadīth in full.

Muslim transmitted it, and it will come in full in al-Ḥashr, if Allah wills.

Tattooing occurs on the hands: it is to pierce the back of a woman's hand and wrist with a needle, then fill it with kohl or with nuʾūr (soot of fat), so that it turns green.

It is said: "washamat tashim washman, so she is wāshimah." Al-mustawshimah is the one on whom this is done. Al-Harawī said this.

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "The men of Sicily and Ifrīqiyya do this, so that each one of them shows his youthful vigor (rujlatuhu) in his youth." (The word is spelled with three vowels on the rāʾ in Ibn al-ʿArabī and in manuscripts ج and ط.)

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: In the narration of al-Harawī, one of Muslim's narrators, in place of (al-wāshimah wa al-mustawshimah) it occurs as (al-wāshiyah wa al-mustawshiyah) (with yāʾ instead of mīm). It is from al-washy, which is embellishment; the root of al-washy is weaving cloth in two colours, and a bull is described as mūashsha (streaked) if its face and legs are black; that is, the woman embellishes herself by what she does to herself of depilation, filing, and the ashr.

Al-mutanammiṣāt is the plural of mutanammiṣah, who plucks hair from her face with the minmās, which is the instrument that pulls out hair; she is also called al-nāmiṣah.

Ibn al-ʿArabī: The people of Egypt pluck pubic hair, and that is part of it, for the Sunnah is shaving the pubic area and plucking the armpit. As for plucking the vulva, it loosens and harms it and destroys much of its benefit.

Al-mutafallijāt is the plural of mutafallijah, who creates the falj (gap) in her teeth, that is, she works at it until one who had closely set teeth by nature has spaced teeth by artifice.

In other than Muslim's book: (al-wāshirāt), which is the plural of wāshirah, the one who files her teeth, that is, makes in them ashr, which are the notches found in the teeth of young people; a grown woman does this in imitation of a young woman.

All these matters have been testified to by the ḥadīths as cursed for the one who does them and as among the major sins.

There was disagreement about the reason for which they were prohibited. It was said: because they belong to the category of deception (tadlīs).

And it was said:

from the category of altering the creation of Allah the Exalted, as Ibn Mas'ud said, and this is the most sound view, and it includes the first meaning.

Then it was said:

This prohibited matter applies only to what is lasting, because it falls under altering the creation of Allah the Exalted. As for what is not lasting, such as kohl and adorning oneself with it for women, the scholars permitted that, Malik and others, and Malik disliked it for men.

Malik also permitted a woman to dye her hands with henna.

It is narrated from Umar that he disapproved of this and said: "Either she dyes both her hands entirely or she leaves it." Malik rejected this narration from Umar, and [he said]: "She should not abandon dyeing with henna, for the Prophet (ﷺ) saw a woman who did not dye and said: 'Do not let any of you leave her hand as if it were a man's hand.' So she continued dyeing until she passed ninety and died."

Qadi Iyad said:

A hadith has come forbidding blackening henna, mentioned by the author of al-Masabih, "and she should not be left bare, and let there be on her neck a necklace of leather thong with beads," for it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said to Aisha [may Allah be pleased with her]:
"It is not fitting that you be without a necklace, whether of thread or of leather thong."

And Anas said:
It is recommended for a woman to hang on her neck during prayer, even if it is only a leather thong.

Abu Ja'far al-Tabari said:
In the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud there is evidence that it is not permissible to change any part of a woman's creation that Allah created her with, by adding or subtracting, seeking beauty for a husband or otherwise, whether she filed her teeth or made them sharp, or had an extra tooth which she removed, or long teeth whose tips she cut.

Likewise, it is not permissible for her to shave a beard, moustache or goatee if such grows on her, because all of that is altering the creation of Allah.

Qadi Iyad said:
And according to what he mentioned, whoever is born with an extra finger or an extra limb may not cut it off or remove it, because it is altering the creation of Allah the Exalted, except that if these extra growths cause him pain, then there is no harm in removing them, according to Abu Ja'far and others.

The eighth [issue]: I say: From this category is his (ﷺ) saying: "Allah has cursed the woman who joins (hair), the woman who has it joined, the woman who tattoos, and the woman who has herself tattooed." Related by Muslim. He (ﷺ) forbade a woman from joining her hair, which is adding other hair to it to make it appear fuller. The "wasilah" is the one who does this, and the "mustawsilah" is the one who asks someone to do it for her. Muslim narrated from Jabir who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade a woman from joining anything to her hair. And [al-Qurtubi] cited from Asma' bint Abi Bakr who said: A woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my daughter is a newlywed [ 'uraysan, diminutive of 'arus] whom measles afflicted so that her hair fell out. Shall I join it?" He said: "Allah has cursed the woman who joins and the woman who has it joined." All of this is explicit text on the prohibition of joining hair, and Malik and the majority of scholars held this view. They prohibited joining with anything of wool, rags, or other things, because it has the same meaning as joining it with hair. Al-Layth ibn Sa'd deviated and permitted joining with wool, rags, and what is not hair, and this is closest to the position of the Zahiris. Others permitted placing hair on the head and said: the prohibition came only regarding joining specifically, and this is pure literalism and disregard of the meaning. A group went to extremes and permitted joining absolutely, which is a view definitively false, rejected by the hadiths. It was narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, but it is not authentic. It was narrated from Ibn Sirin that a man asked him: "My mother used to comb women's hair; do you think I eat from her wealth?" He said: "If she used to join, then no." The prohibition does not include what is tied with colored silk threads for the purpose of adornment and beautification, and Allah knows best.

The ninth [issue]: A group said: The meaning of altering the creation of Allah is that Allah the Exalted created the sun, the moon, the stones, the fire and other creatures so that they would be considered and benefited from, and the disbelievers altered them by making them worshipped gods. Al-Zajjaj said: Allah the Exalted created livestock to be ridden and eaten, and they forbade them to themselves, and He made the sun, the moon and the stones subservient to people, and they made them gods to worship; thus they altered what Allah created. This was said by a group of exegetes: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: "then they will change the creation of Allah" means "the religion of Allah," and al-Nakha'i said it, and al-Tabari chose it. He said: If that is its meaning, then it includes every act Allah has forbidden, such as castration, tattooing and other sins, because Satan calls to all sins; that is, "then they will change what Allah created in His religion." Mujahid also said: "then they will change the creation of Allah" means the fitrah of Allah upon which He created people, meaning that they were born upon Islam, and Satan commanded them to change it. This is the meaning of his (ﷺ) saying: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, and his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian." So the meaning of creation returns to what He placed in them on the Day of the Covenant of faith in Him, in His saying: "Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes" (see vol. 7, p. 314). Ibn al-Arabi said: It was narrated from Tawus that he would not attend the marriage of a black woman to a white man, or a white woman to a black man, and he would say: this is from the saying of Allah: "then they will change the creation of Allah." The Qadi said: Although the wording may allow this, it is specific to what the Prophet (ﷺ) carried out in marrying his freedman Zayd, who was white, to his wet-nurse Barakah the Abyssinian, mother of Usama, who was black, a white man to a black woman; and this was hidden from Tawus despite his knowledge. I say: Then Usama married Fatimah bint Qays, who was white and Qurashi. And Barakah was once under Bilal, sister of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who was Zuhri. This also is specific, and it was hidden from both of them.

The meaning: he promises them his falsehoods and deceptions, of wealth, status and leadership, and that there will be no resurrection and no punishment. He makes them fear poverty so that they will not spend in good causes. ﴿And so he promises them﴾ ﴿and Satan promises them only delusion﴾, that is, deception. Ibn 'Arafa said: Delusion (ghurur) is what you see as something apparently good that you love, while inwardly it is something hateful or unknown. Satan is a source of delusion, because he drives people toward what the self desires, and behind that lies what will harm them.

﴿Those﴾ is the inchoative subject (mubtada'). ﴿Their refuge﴾ is a second inchoative subject. ﴿Hell﴾ is the predicate of the second, and the whole clause is the predicate of the first. ﴿Refuge (mahis)﴾ means a place of shelter, and its verb is ḥāṣa, yaḥīṣu.

﴿And who is more truthful than God in speech?﴾ is an inchoative subject and predicate.

﴿Speech (qīlan)﴾ is in the accusative as a specification (tamyīz). He said qīlan, qawlan and qālan, with the same meaning: there is no one more truthful than God. The discussion of what these verses contain of meanings has already passed, and praise belongs to God.

**Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾.** Abu Ja'far al-Madani read (*laysa bi-amaniyyikum wa la amani ahl al-kitab*) with the *ya'* lightened (*takhfif*) in both places.

Among the best reports about its revelation is what al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Jews and the Christians said, "None will enter the Garden except those who are of us." The Quraysh said, "There is no resurrection (*laysa nub'ath*)." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: The believers and the People of the Book boasted to one another. The People of the Book said, "Our prophet came before your prophet, our scripture came before your scripture, and we have more right to Allah than you do." The believers said, "Our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our scripture overrides all the other scriptures." Then the verse was revealed.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. Here "evil" (*su'*) means polytheism (*shirk*). Al-Hasan said: This verse concerns the disbeliever. He recited (*wa-hal yujaza illa al-kafur*, "And is any recompensed but the ungrateful?"), which is the reading of Nafi'. (See vol. 14, p. 288.)

Also from al-Hasan: "(Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it)" refers to the one whom Allah wills to humiliate; as for the one whom He wills to honour, it does not apply to him. Allah has mentioned a people and said: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds; they are among the companions of the Garden, a true promise which they were promised﴾.

Al-Dahhak said: It means the Jews, the Christians, the Magians and the disbelieving Arabs.

The majority (*al-jumhur*) said: The wording of the verse is general. The disbeliever and the believer are both recompensed for their evil deeds. As for the recompense of the disbeliever, it is the Fire, because his disbelief encompasses him. As for the believer, it is through the afflictions of this world, as Muslim related in his Sahih from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the verse (*man ya'mal su'an yujza bihi*) was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be steadfast and strive to be upright, for in everything by which a Muslim is afflicted there is expiation, even the prick he is pricked by and the thorn that pricks him."

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim also reported in *Nawadir al-Usul*, in the ninety-fifth chapter: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamirr al-Hudhali told us, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan (it is narrated with *ya'* and with *ba'*, per *al-Taqrib*) Abu Zayd told us, who said: I heard my father narrate from his father, who said: "I accompanied Ibn Umar from Makkah to Madinah. He said to Nafi': 'Do not pass me by the crucified one,' meaning Ibn al-Zubayr." He said: "Then in the middle of the night, suddenly (*fajaahu*) his mount's trunk (*jidh'uhu*) struck him, so he sat up, wiped his eyes, and said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, Abu Khubayb! If you were... and if you were...! I heard your father al-Zubayr say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world or in the Hereafter." So if this is with that, then *hihih*.'"

Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Abd Allah, said: As for the Revelation, it stated it in general terms: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper﴾. Thus the righteous and the wicked, the enemy and the ally, the believer and the disbeliever are all included. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in this hadith distinguished between the two abodes, saying: "He will be recompensed for it in this world or in the Hereafter." The recompense is not gathered for him in both abodes. Do you not see that Ibn Umar said: "So if this is with that, then *hihih*"? Its meaning is that he fought within the sanctuary of Allah and committed a great offence in it, until the House was burnt and the Black Stone was struck by the catapult (*minjaniq*) and split, until it was bound with silver, and it remains so to this day. The House was heard to moan: "Ah, ah!" When Ibn Umar saw his deed, and then saw him killed and crucified, he remembered the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it." Then he said: "If this killing is with that which he did, then *hihih*," meaning: as though he was recompensed for that evil with this killing and crucifixion. May Allah have mercy on him!

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distinguished between the two groups in another hadith: My father told us, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: Abu Nu'aym told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Usamah ibn al-Had al-Laythi, who said: "When the verse (*man ya'mal su'an yujza bihi*) was revealed, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'This does not leave any of us unscathed.' He said: 'O Abu Bakr, the believer is only recompensed for it in this world, and the disbeliever will be recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Al-Jarud told us, who said: Waki' and Abu Mu'awiyah and Abdah (he is Ibn Sulayman al-Kilabi, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, per *al-Tahdhib*) told us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Bakr ibn [Abi] Zuhayr (Abu Zuhayr is Mu'adh ibn Rabah al-Thaqafi, as in *Usd al-Ghabah*; in *al-Tahdhib* it is Abu Zuhrah) al-Thaqafi, who said: "When the verse (*man ya'mal su'an yujza bihi*) was revealed, Abu Bakr said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how can there be righteousness with this? Every deed we do, we are recompensed for.' He said: 'May Allah forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer hardship (*al-la'wa'*)?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'That is what you are recompensed for.' Thus the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained what the Revelation had stated in general terms in his saying: 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.'"

Al-Tirmidhi related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that when it was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and the believers, you are recompensed for it in this world until you meet Allah with no sins. As for the others, it is accumulated for them until they are recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "It is a gharib hadith; there is some criticism in its chain. Musa ibn Ubaydah is weak in hadith; Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan and Ahmad ibn Hanbal declared him weak. The mawla of Ibn Sibá' is unknown. This has been related through another route from Abu Bakr, but it does not have a sound chain either. On this subject there is also a report from A'ishah." I say: Isma'il ibn Ishaq al-Qadi related it, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, who said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Ali ibn Yazid, from his mother, that she asked A'ishah about this verse (*wa-in tubdu ma fi anfusikum aw tukhfuhu*) and about this verse (*man ya'mal su'an yujza bihi*). A'ishah said: "No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. He said: 'O A'ishah, this is the sin-recompense of Allah for what befalls a person: fever, misfortune, and thorn-prick, even the merchandise that he places in his sleeve and then loses, so he is alarmed, then finds it in his bag. Indeed, the believer comes out of his sins just as the gold comes out of the furnace.'"

The subject (*ism*) of *laysa* is implied in all of these sayings, and the sense is: "It is not what you wish for that will happen among your affairs, but whoever does evil will be recompensed for it." It was also said: The meaning is: the reward of Allah is not by your wishful thinking, since it has already been mentioned: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall admit them into Gardens﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾, meaning the polytheists, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We shall help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ (see vol. 15, p. 322). It was also said: (*man ya'mal su'an yujza bihi*) except that he repents.

The reading of the community (*qira'at al-jama'ah*) is (*wa-la yajid lahu*) with *jazm* (the apocopate), coordinated (*'atfan*) upon (*yujza bihi*). Ibn Bakkar related from Ibn Amir (*wa-la yajidu*) with *raf'* as a new clause (*isti'nafan*). If the verse is understood as referring to the disbeliever, then tomorrow he will have no protector or helper. If it is understood as referring to the believer, then he will have no protector or helper apart from Allah.

This passage is about 4:124, which reads: "Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the speck in a date-pit."

He made faith a condition because the polytheists claimed merit through serving the Ka'bah, feeding the pilgrims, and hospitality to guests, and the People of the Book claimed merit through their priority (in time) and their saying, "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved." So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that good deeds are not accepted without faith.

Ash-Shaykhan, Abu 'Amr and Ibn Kathir, recited "yudkhalūna al-jannata" (with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatḥah on the khā'), in the passive form, the subject not being named (ʿalā mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu). The rest read it with a fatḥah on the yā' and a ḍammah on the khā', meaning they enter Paradise by their deeds.

The naqīr (نَقِير) has already been mentioned: it is the small pit or notch on the back of a date-stone (al-nuktah fī ẓahr al-nawāh), used as an image of the smallest measure.

قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ دِيناً مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ وَاتَّبَعَ مِلَّةَ إِبْراهِيمَ حَنِيفاً﴾ *[And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth.]* فَضَّلَ دِينَ الْإِسْلَامِ عَلَى سَائِرِ الْأَدْيَانِ. وَ(أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ) مَعْنَاهُ أَخْلَصَ دِينَهُ لِلَّهِ وَخَضَعَ لَهُ وَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَيْهِ بِالْعِبَادَةِ. قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: أَرَادَ أَبَا بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ. وَانْتَصَبَ (دِيناً) عَلَى الْبَيَانِ *[i.e., as a specification/explanatory accusative (tamyiz)]*.

(وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ): ابْتِدَاءٌ *[subject (mubtada')]* وَخَبَرٌ *[predicate (khabar)]* فِي مَوْضِعِ الْحَالِ، أَيْ مُوَحِّدٌ، فَلَا يَدْخُلُ فِيهِ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ، لِأَنَّهُمْ تَرَكُوا الْإِيمَانَ بِمُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ. وَالْمِلَّةُ الدِّينُ، وَالْحَنِيفُ الْمُسْلِمُ وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ [[راجع ج ٢ ص ١٣٩]].

قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلًا﴾ *[And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.]* قَالَ ثَعْلَبٌ: إِنَّمَا سُمِّيَ الْخَلِيلُ خَلِيلًا لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّتَهُ تَتَخَلَّلُ الْقَلْبَ فَلَا تَدَعُ فِيهِ خَلَلًا إِلَّا مَلَأَتْهُ، وَأَنْشَدَ قَوْلَ بَشَّارٍ:

*You have penetrated the passage of my spirit,*
*And by this the khalil was named khalil.*

وَخَلِيلٌ فَعِيلٌ بِمَعْنَى فَاعِلٍ، كَالْعَلِيمِ بِمَعْنَى الْعَالِمِ. وَقِيلَ: هُوَ [بِمَعْنَى] الْمَفْعُولِ، كَالْحَبِيبِ بِمَعْنَى الْمَحْبُوبِ، وَإِبْرَاهِيمُ كَانَ مُحِبًّا لِلَّهِ وَكَانَ مَحْبُوبًا [لِلَّهِ [[من ج.]]]. وَقِيلَ: الْخَلِيلُ مِنَ الِاخْتِصَاصِ، فَاللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَعْلَمُ اخْتَصَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي وَقْتِهِ لِلرِّسَالَةِ. وَاخْتَارَ هَذَا النَّحَّاسُ قَالَ: وَالدَّلِيلُ عَلَى هَذَا قَوْلُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ: (وَقَدِ اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ صَاحِبَكُمْ خَلِيلًا) يَعْنِي نَفْسَهُ. وَقَالَ ﷺ: (لَوْ كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذًا خَلِيلًا لَاتَّخَذْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ خَلِيلًا)، أَيْ لَوْ كُنْتُ مُخْتَصًّا أَحَدًا بِشَيْءٍ لَاخْتَصَصْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ. وَفِي هَذَا رَدٌّ عَلَى مَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ اخْتَصَّ بَعْضَ أَصْحَابِهِ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الدِّينِ. وَقِيلَ: الْخَلِيلُ الْمُحْتَاجُ، فَإِبْرَاهِيمُ خَلِيلُ اللَّهِ عَلَى مَعْنَى أَنَّهُ فَقِيرٌ مُحْتَاجٌ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى، كَأَنَّهُ الَّذِي بِهِ الِاخْتِلَالُ. وَقَالَ زُهَيْرٌ يَمْدَحُ هَرِمَ بْنَ سِنَانٍ:

*And if a khalil comes to him on a day of hunger,*
*he says: "No one prevails over my wealth, nor is it forbidden."*

أَيْ لَا مَمْنُوعٌ. قَالَ الزَّجَّاجُ: وَمَعْنَى الْخَلِيلِ: الَّذِي لَيْسَ فِي مَحَبَّتِهِ خَلَلٌ، فَجَائِزٌ أَنْ يَكُونَ سُمِّيَ خَلِيلًا لِلَّهِ بِأَنَّهُ الَّذِي أَحَبَّهُ وَاصْطَفَاهُ مَحَبَّةً تَامَّةً. وَجَائِزٌ أَنْ يُسَمَّى خَلِيلَ اللَّهِ، أَيْ فَقِيرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى، لِأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ فَقْرَهُ وَلَا فَاقَتَهُ إِلَّا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى مُخْلِصًا فِي ذَلِكَ. وَالِاخْتِلَالُ الْفَقْرُ. فَرُوِيَ أَنَّهُ لَمَّا رُمِيَ بِالْمَنْجَنِيقِ وَصَارَ فِي الْهَوَاءِ أَتَاهُ جِبْرِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَقَالَ: أَلَكَ حَاجَةٌ؟ قَالَ: أَمَّا إِلَيْكَ فَلَا. فَخُلَّةُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى لِإِبْرَاهِيمَ نُصْرَتُهُ إِيَّاهُ. وَقِيلَ: سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ بِسَبَبِ أَنَّهُ مَضَى إِلَى خَلِيلٍ لَهُ بِمِصْرَ، وَقِيلَ: بِالْمَوْصِلِ، لِيَمْتَارَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ طَعَامًا فَلَمْ يَجِدْ صَاحِبَهُ، فَمَلَأَ غَرَائِرَهُ رَمْلًا وَرَاحَ بِهِ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ فَحَطَّهُ وَنَامَ، فَفَتَحَهُ أَهْلُهُ فَوَجَدُوهُ دَقِيقًا فَصَنَعُوا لَهُ مِنْهُ، فَلَمَّا قَدَّمُوهُ إِلَيْهِ قَالَ: مِنْ أَيْنَ لَكُمْ هَذَا؟ قَالُوا: مِنَ الَّذِي جِئْتَ بِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِ خَلِيلِكَ الْمِصْرِيِّ، فَقَالَ: هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ خَلِيلِي، يَعْنِي اللَّهَ تَعَالَى، فَسُمِّيَ خَلِيلَ اللَّهِ بِذَلِكَ. وَقِيلَ: إِنَّهُ أَضَافَ رُؤَسَاءَ الْكُفَّارِ وَأَهْدَى لَهُمْ هَدَايَا وَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِمْ، فَقَالُوا لَهُ: مَا حَاجَتُكَ؟ قَالَ: حَاجَتِي أَنْ تَسْجُدُوا سَجْدَةً، فَسَجَدُوا، فَدَعَا اللَّهَ تَعَالَى وَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي قَدْ فَعَلْتُ مَا أَمْكَنَنِي فَافْعَلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَنْتَ أَهْلٌ لِذَلِكَ، فَوَفَّقَهُمُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لِلْإِسْلَامِ، فَاتَّخَذَهُ اللَّهُ خَلِيلًا لِذَلِكَ. وَيُقَالُ: لَمَّا دَخَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ بِشَبَهِ الْآدَمِيِّينَ وَجَاءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ فَلَمْ يَأْكُلُوا مِنْهُ وَقَالُوا: إِنَّا لَا نَأْكُلُ شَيْئًا بِغَيْرِ ثَمَنٍ، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ: أَعْطُوا ثَمَنَهُ وَكُلُوا، قَالُوا: وَمَا ثَمَنُهُ؟ قَالَ: أَنْ تَقُولُوا فِي أَوَّلِهِ بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ وَفِي آخِرِهِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، فَقَالُوا فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمْ: حَقٌّ عَلَى اللَّهِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَهُ خَلِيلًا، فَاتَّخَذَهُ اللَّهُ خَلِيلًا. وَرَوَى جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: (اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلًا لِإِطْعَامِهِ الطَّعَامَ وَإِفْشَائِهِ السَّلَامَ وَصَلَاتِهِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّاسُ نِيَامٌ). وَرَوَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: (يَا جِبْرِيلُ لِمَ اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلًا؟) قَالَ: لِإِطْعَامِهِ الطَّعَامَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ. وَقِيلَ: مَعْنَى الْخَلِيلِ الَّذِي يُوَالِي فِي اللَّهِ وَيُعَادِي فِي اللَّهِ. وَالْخُلَّةُ بَيْنَ الْآدَمِيِّينَ الصَّدَاقَةُ، مُشْتَقَّةٌ مِنْ تَخَلُّلِ الْأَسْرَارِ بَيْنَ الْمُتَخَالِّينَ. وَقِيلَ: هِيَ مِنَ الْخَلَّةِ، فَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَ الْخَلِيلَيْنِ يَسُدُّ خَلَّةَ صَاحِبِهِ. وَفِي مُصَنَّفِ أَبِي دَاوُدَ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: (الرَّجُلُ عَلَى دِينِ خَلِيلِهِ فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَحَدُكُمْ مَنْ يُخَالِلْ). وَلَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ مَنْ قَالَ:

*Whoever has no friendship with him in God,*
*his friend is at risk from him.*

آخَرُ:

*When you intend to take a khalil,*
*do not trust every brother of brotherhood.*
*If you are given a choice among them, cling*
*to the people of intellect and modesty among them.*
*For intellect has no equal*
*when virtues are weighed against one another.*

وَقَالَ حَسَّانُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ:

*The friends of men are many,*
*but in trials they are few.*
*Let the friendship of one who claims brotherhood not deceive you,*
*for you will have no friend at a time of calamity.*
*Every brother says, "I am faithful,"*
*but he does not do what he says.*
*Except a friend who has lineage and religion,*
*he is the one who does what he says.*

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 126:

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ means: in ownership and origination (ikhtira').

The meaning is that He took Ibrahim as a khalil (intimate friend) on account of his good obedience, not because He had need of his friendship, nor for the sake of multiplying through him or strengthening Himself by him. And how could that be, when to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? Rather, He honoured him because of his compliance with His command.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing﴾ means: His knowledge has encompassed all things.

The Qur'an was revealed because some of the Companions (Sahabah) asked about the matters of women and their rulings concerning inheritance and other things. So God commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to say to them [[from ṭ.]]: "God gives you a ruling concerning them", that is, He will make clear to you the ruling on what you asked about. This verse refers back to what the surah opened with regarding the matter of women, and some rulings remained that they did not know, so they asked, and it was said to them: "Indeed God gives you a ruling concerning them." Ashhab narrated from Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to be asked and would not answer until revelation came down to him, and that is in the Book of God: (They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them).

(They ask you concerning orphans) [[See vol. 3 pp. 6 and 51.]]. And (They ask you concerning wine and gambling) [[See vol. 3 pp. 6 and 51.]].

(They ask you concerning the mountains) [[See vol. 11 p. 245.]].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what is recited to you﴾. The word "mā" (what) is in the nominative position, conjoined to the name of God, exalted is He. The meaning is: and the Qur'an gives you a ruling concerning them, and that is His saying: (So marry what seems good to you of women) [[See p. 12 and what follows it of this part.]]. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ means: and you desire to refrain from marrying them, then the word "ʿan" (from) was omitted.

It was also said: and you desire to marry them, meaning you desire in marrying them, then the word "fi" (in) was omitted. Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: "and one is inclined to marry them when they are wealthy." The hadith of ʿAʾishah strengthens the omission of "ʿan," for in her hadith: "and you desire to marry them out of the desire of one of you to refrain from his orphan under his guardianship when she is poor in wealth and beauty," and it has been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

There are seven issues in this. The first concerns His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment (nushuz) or aversion﴾. The word ﴿امرأة﴾ (imra'a, "woman") is in the nominative, governed by an implied verb that the following clause explains. The word ﴿خافت﴾ (khafat, "feared") here means "anticipated." The view of those who say it means "was certain" is wrong. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "and if a woman fears from her husband the persistence of nushuz." Al-Nahhas said: the difference between nushuz and i'rad (aversion) is that nushuz is distancing oneself, while i'rad is not speaking to her and not being friendly with her.

The verse was revealed concerning Sawda bint Zam'a. At-Tirmidhi related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Sawda feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would divorce her, so she said: "Do not divorce me, keep me, and give my day to 'A'isha." He did so, and then the verse was revealed: ﴿There is no blame on them both if they make a settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾. Whatever the two agreed upon is permissible. He said: this is a hadith that is ḥasan gharib (good and strange).

Ibn 'Uyayna related from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Rafi' ibn Khadij had a wife, Khawla, the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslama. He disliked something about her, whether due to her age or something else, and wanted to divorce her. She said: "Do not divorce me, and divide the nights as you wish." So the practice was established accordingly, and the verse was revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband nushuz or i'rad﴾.

Al-Bukhari related from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband nushuz or i'rad﴾, that she said: "A man has a woman who is not greatly desired by him, and he wants to separate from her, so she says: 'I release you from any obligation regarding me.' Then this verse was revealed." The common reading is ﴿أن يصالحا﴾ (an yuṣāliḥā, "that they settle").

Most of the Kufans read ﴿أن يُصلحا﴾ (an yuṣliḥā). Al-Jahdari and 'Uthman al-Batti read ﴿أن يَصَّلِحا﴾ (an yaṣṣaliḥā), meaning yaṣṭaliḥā, and then it was assimilated.

The second issue: this verse contains a refutation of the foolish ignorant ones who think that if a man takes the youth of a woman and she grows old, he should not replace her. Ibn Abi Mulayka said: when Sawda bint Zam'a grew old, the Prophet ﷺ wanted to divorce her, but she preferred to remain with him, and said to him: "Keep me and give my day (nawbati) to 'A'isha." He ﷺ did so. She died while still among his wives.

I say: Likewise did the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslama. Malik related from Ibn Shihab, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, that he married the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansariyya. She remained with him until she grew old, then he married a young girl and preferred the young girl over her. She asked him for divorce, so he divorced her once. Then he left her until her waiting period was about to end, and he took her back. Then he returned to preferring the young girl, and she asked him for divorce again, so he divorced her once. Then he took her back, and again he preferred the young girl, and she asked for divorce. He said: "What do you want? Only one (divorce) remains. If you wish, you may remain with what you see of preference (ithra), or if you wish, I will part from you." She said: "Rather, I will remain with the preference." So he kept her on that basis, and Rafi' saw no sin upon him when she stayed with him despite the preference. Ma'mar related it from al-Zuhri with its wording and meaning, and added: "That is the settlement which we have been told was revealed concerning it: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband nushuz or i'rad, there is no blame on them both if they make a settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾."

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: his saying, and Allah knows best, "he preferred the young girl over her," means in inclination of the heart toward her and eagerness for her, not that he preferred her over her in food, clothing, or lodging, because this should not be attributed to a man like Rafi'. And Allah knows best.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba mentioned, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man asked him about this verse, and he said: "It concerns the woman who is with a man, and his eyes turn away from her because of her plainness, poverty, old age, or bad character, and she dislikes separation from him. If she gives him something of her dower, it is permissible for him to take it, and if she gives him some of her days, there is no harm." Ad-Dahhak said: "There is no harm if he reduces her share of her rights when he marries one who is younger and more pleasing to him." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "It concerns the man who has an older woman under him, and he marries a young woman over her, and says to this older woman: 'I will give you from my wealth on condition that I divide the nights and days with this young woman more than I divide with you.' So the other agrees to what they have settled upon. If she refuses and does not accept, then he must be just between them in the division."

The third issue: our scholars said: in this matter, all kinds of settlement are permitted in this situation, whether the husband gives something on condition that she be patient, or she gives something on condition that the husband prefers her (or on condition that she prefers the husband, or on condition that she keeps the marriage bond), or the settlement takes place on patience and preference without any payment. All of this is permitted. It is also permissible for one of them to settle with the other concerning her day in exchange for something she gives her, as the wives of the Prophet ﷺ did. That is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had become angry with Safiyya, so she said to 'A'isha: "Reconcile between me and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I have given my day to you." Ibn Khuwayz Mindad mentioned it in his Ahkam from 'A'isha, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was displeased with Safiyya over something. Safiyya said to me: 'Would you like to make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pleased with me, and you will have my day?' She said: So I put on a headscarf I had, dyed with saffron, and sprinkled it with perfume, then I came and sat beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: '(Move) away from me, for this is not your day.' I said: 'That is the bounty of Allah, He gives it to whom He wills,' and I informed him of the matter, and he was pleased with her."

In this is that leaving equal treatment among the wives and preferring some of them over others is not permissible except with the permission and consent of the one who is disfavored.

The fourth issue: the Kufans read ﴿يُصلِحا﴾ (yuṣliḥā), and the rest read ﴿أن يَصَّالَحا﴾ (an yaṣṣālaḥā). Al-Jahdari read ﴿يَصَّلِحا﴾ (yaṣṣaliḥā). As for the one who reads ﴿يَصَّالَحا﴾ (yaṣṣālaḥā), his reasoning is that the common usage in Arabic, when there is a dispute between people, is to say: "taṣāla'a al-qawm" (the people reconciled), and not "aṣlaḥa al-qawm." And if it were aṣlaḥa, its verbal noun would be iṣlāḥ. As for the one who reads ﴿يُصلِحا﴾ (yuṣliḥā), he has used a similar form for dispute and contention, as He said: ﴿فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ (fa-aṣlaḥa baynahum, "and he made peace between them"). In this reading, ﴿يُصلِحا﴾ (yuṣliḥā) is in the accusative as an object, and ṣulḥ (settlement) is a noun like 'aṭā' (gift) from a'ṭaytu. So aṣlaḥtu ṣulḥan is like aṣlaḥtu amran (I put a matter right). Likewise it is an object in the reading of the one who reads ﴿يَصَّالَحا﴾ (yaṣṣālaḥā), because tafā'ala has come transitively, and it may be a verbal noun whose extra letters were dropped. As for the one who reads ﴿يُصلِحا﴾ (yuṣliḥā), the original form is yaṣtaliḥā, then it became yaṣṭaliḥā, then the ṭā' was changed to ṣād and the ṣād was assimilated into it, and the ṣād was not changed to ṭā' because of the prolonged breath in it.

The fifth issue: His words, may He be exalted: ﴿وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾ (and settlement is best) is a general and absolute expression, requiring that true settlement, by which souls find tranquility and disagreement is removed, is best absolutely. This meaning includes everything over which a settlement takes place between a man and his wife, whether concerning property, intercourse, or other matters.

(Khayr, "best," means: better than separation, for persisting in disagreement, enmity, and hatred are the roots of evil.) The Prophet ﷺ said about hatred: "It is the shaver," meaning the shaver of the religion, not the shaver of hair.

The sixth issue: His words, may He be exalted: ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ﴾ (and souls are present with stinginess) is information that stinginess is present in everyone, and that a person must be stingy by the nature of his creation and disposition, to the extent that he may compel his companion to some of what he dislikes. It is said: shaḥḥa yashuḥḥu (with kasra on the shīn), i.e. "shuḥḥ" (stinginess) is a noun for it. Ibn Jubayr said: it is the wife's stinginess regarding maintenance from her husband and his division of time for her days. Ibn Zayd said: stinginess here is from him and from her. Ibn 'Aṭiyya said: "This is the best view, for what prevails in a woman is stinginess regarding her share from her husband, and what prevails in a husband is stinginess regarding his share from the young wife." Shuḥḥ (stinginess) is restraint over beliefs, will, aspirations, wealth, and the like. What exceeds it in matters of religion is praiseworthy, and what exceeds it in other matters contains some blame, and this is what Allah refers to when He says: ﴿وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ (And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, it is those who are the successful). What reaches the domain of withholding legal rights, or what the manliness (muru'a) requires, is miserliness (bukhl), and it is a vice. When miserliness leads to these blameworthy character traits and base dispositions, no hoped-for good remains with it, and no expected righteousness.

I say: It has been related that the Prophet ﷺ said to the Ansar: "Who is your chief?" They said: "Al-Jadd ibn Qays, but he has some miserliness." The Prophet ﷺ said: "And what disease is more harmful than miserliness!" They said: "How so, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "A people settled by the seashore, and out of their miserliness they disliked the arrival of guests among them. So they said: 'Let the men keep away from the women, so that the men may excuse themselves to the guests by the distance of the women, and the women excuse themselves by the distance of the men.' They did so, and this continued for them, so the men became occupied with men and the women with women." Al-Mawardi has previously mentioned this.

The seventh issue: His words, may He be exalted: ﴿وَإِن تُحْسِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ (And if you do good and fear Allah) is the condition, and ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted) is its response. This is an address to the husbands, since the husband may be stingy and not do good. That is, if you do good and fear Allah in treating women well, by remaining with them despite your dislike of their company, and by guarding against wronging them, then it is better for you.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 129:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely [away from one]﴾. He, exalted is He, informed that they have no ability to be equitable between wives. This refers to the natural inclination of the heart through affection, intimacy (al-jima') and the portion of the heart. Thus Allah, exalted is He, described the state of human beings: that by their natural creation they do not possess control over their hearts' inclination toward some over others. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, used to say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not control." Then He forbade, saying: "So do not incline completely [away from one]." Mujahid said: Do not intentionally wrong them; rather, hold to equality in the division (of time) and in maintenance, for this is what is within one's ability. The explanation of this will come in detail, God willing, in (al-Ahzab [[See vol. 14, p. 214]]). Qatadah narrated from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has two wives and does not treat them equitably will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of him leaning."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So you leave her as if suspended﴾. That is, she is neither divorced nor a married woman; this is what al-Hasan said. This is a simile with something suspended from something, for it has settled neither on the ground nor on that from which it is hung. This is consistent with their proverb: "Be content with the rider's position by hanging" (irdi min al-markab bil-ta'liq). In the terminology of the grammarians, (min) is [[in the editions: in ta'liq]] the suspension of the verb. And from it, in the hadith of Umm Zar'; in the woman's words: "My husband is al-'Ashannaq [[al-'Ashannaq: the tall, long-statured one; she meant that he has an appearance without substance]], if I speak he divorces me, and if I remain silent I am left suspended." Qatadah said: "like one imprisoned," and thus Ubayy recited (so you leave her as one imprisoned). Ibn Mas'ud recited (so you leave her as if she were suspended). The position of (fa-tadharuha) is in the accusative, because it is the answer to the prohibition. And the kaf in (ka'l-mu'allaqah) is also in the accusative position.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 4, verse 130–132:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾. That is, if they do not reconcile but separate, then let each of them think well of Allah, for a man may be granted a wife who gladdens his eye, and a woman may be granted one who provides abundantly for her. It is narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad that a man complained to him of poverty, so he ordered him to marry. The man went and married, then came back to him complaining of poverty, so he ordered him to divorce. He was asked about this verse and said: "I ordered him to marry because he may be among the people of this verse: (If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty) [[See vol. 12, p. 241.]]. When he was not among the people of that verse, I ordered him to divorce, and I said: then perhaps he is among the people of this verse: (But if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance)."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you﴾. That is, the command to piety was general for all nations. The discussion of taqwa (piety, God-consciousness) has already passed [[See vol. 1, p. 161.]].

(﴿And you﴾) is conjoined to (﴿those﴾).

(﴿That fear Allah﴾) is in a position of accusative (naṣb). Al-Akhfash said: that is, "bi-anne" (that), i.e., "that fear Allah." Some of the knowers (ʿārifīn) said: this verse is the millstone (raḥā) of the verses of the Qur'an, for the whole of it revolves around it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy. And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾. If someone says: what is the benefit of this repetition? There are two answers to this. The first: it was repeated for emphasis, so that the servants would take heed and reflect on what is in His dominion and kingdom, and that He is free of need of the worlds. The second answer: it was repeated for several benefits. In the first, He informed that Allah, Exalted is He, enriches each of them from His abundance, because to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so His treasures never run out. Then He said: We have enjoined you and the People of the Book to fear Allah, (﴿And if you disbelieve﴾) [i.e., and if you disbelieve], then indeed He is free of need of you, because to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Then in the third, He informed of His preserving His creation and managing them by His saying: (﴿and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾), because to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And He said (﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾) and did not say (﴿who is in the heavens﴾), because He took it in the sense of a genus, and in the heavens and the earth there are those who reason and those who do not.
